56afd259-0505-5d2d-b7f1-9be15cb0dea2.definition: Arabic dynasty that initially ruled over most of the Islamic empire after assuming the caliphate in 750 CE.

137730df-6e0e-5520-b259-aa4bde8cd222.definition: Abd al-Samad, an Iranian artist born approximately between AH 910 / AD 1505 and AH 920 / AD 1515 in Shiraz, received his artistic training at the royal workshop of Shah Tahmasp in Tabriz. He had a distinguished career, spanning from the AH 936 / AD 1530s until his passing in around AH 1008 / AD 1600. Abd al-Samad was a highly skilled artist with his roots in Safavid Iran. Initially, he served under Shah Tahmasp, who reigned from AH 930- 983 / AD 1524 to 1576 at Tabriz. Later, he was enlisted by the Mughal emperor-in-exile, Humayun.  Staring from AH 956 / AD 1549, 'Abd al-Samad, Alongside two other renowned Iranian court painters, Miravvir and his son Mir Sayyid 'Ali, served Humayun at his exiled court in Kabul.

e2af48f9-49cb-51b7-84fd-bbcca177f07b.definition:
Masonry technique used in facades of historical buildings and characterised by alternating rows of light (yellow or white) and dark (red or black) stones or bricks.  
  
The first fortress built in this style in northern Arabia during the 5th century AD was the fortress of Samawal. The style spread from al-Andalus, specifically from the Great Mosque of Cordoba (AH 170 / AD 776) into Islamic architecture. It became popular in the Levant due to the availability of white limestone and black basalt. A notable example is the Azem (or Ablaq) Palace in Damascus. Examples in Cairo include Khanqah Baybars al-Jashankir and the mosque built by Sultan Al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun.

8e22eece-aa71-5c15-9776-799a90bed70e.definition: A practice of ritual cleansing with water to be performed before prayer.

c94f90f7-949a-50b0-93a1-337d3f7e80bf.definition: Abu Zayd Kashani was an Iranian ceramicist, painter, calligrapher, and poet from the late 6th to early 7th century AH (late 12th to early 13th century AD). Abu Zayd is one of the most renowned ceramic artists from before the Mongol era, producing exquisite Minai and Zarrin-faam (gilded) ceramics over an extended period from 582 to 616 AH (1186-1219 AD). His works are considered among the earliest and most significant historical examples in the field of Iranian ceramics.

ee146c66-d28a-545e-ba9f-fbf2e523c6a5.definition: An ancient city in Algeria, first capital of the Muslim dynasty of the Zirids.

870f1783-fcfb-57f0-806e-5a4684d21fb7.definition: Call to prayer. Tr. *ezan*. See also *muezzin*.

199be476-a6fb-5584-8c39-6af25455b9be.definition: A paper-treating process. Paper that was to be used for calligraphy had to be treated to prevent the ink from spreading. The paper was sized (*ahar*) with a special solution to obtain a very smooth surface.

84e97899-231d-5674-b71e-5b985f91973b.definition: A decorative historical interior design technique and remains one of Syria’s best known handcrafts. The word itself describes different elements of the craft: from the act of applying relief paste to a plain surface, to the resulting ornamentation. Ajami also describes the type of room cladded with these artfully painted wooden panels. It is often complemented by the so called opus sectile works and complex carvings.

85a0ff83-d0ac-53f5-8e2f-e782ef2dbb2b.definition: An official chronicle of the reign of Akbar, the Akbarnama is a collection of texts and illustrated manuscripts written in Farsi by the court historian and biographer Abu’l Fazl ibn Mubarak and commissioned by Akbar himself. Composed between 1590 and 1597 CE, the manuscript consists of 274 folios of text interspersed with 116 illustrated folios and one illuminated front piece.

34f3c711-7719-5478-a311-2b54051f81d0.definition: One of the 99 names of God, meaning The Just, fair.

7e65a713-3deb-5ac1-94da-c18827b66bd0.definition: The 33rd Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Confederates". It is consisted of 73 verses.

b80f901c-a916-59e9-aef8-0417192fcbbe.definition: One of the 99 names of God, meaning The Sublime, ever exalted, supreme, The Exalted.

178f1fa5-283a-5cf8-8b24-7ea872bd9ccd.definition: One of the 99 names of God meaning The Knowing, all knowing, The Knower.

b167cfe8-dff2-5e19-ba87-f3396f0af125.definition: The 6th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Cattle". It is composed of 165 verses.

c44302b7-5b2a-5247-b1b7-8c1a06993aa4.definition: The 2nd Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Cow". It is composed of 286 verses.

ff459676-63f5-5f92-bb0c-69743e22e7fc.definition: The 85th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Mansions of the Stars". It is composed of 22 verses.

747e800c-2146-5632-889b-02f277a7ec61.definition: From the Arabic word *Dawla*, meaning to turn, alternate, or come around in a cyclical fashion. The sense of alternating periods of fortune or misfortune led Arab writers to use the word when speaking of dynastic succession. In the 19th century, as Western distinctions between the state and the government began to filter into Muslim countries, Dawla became increasingly disentangled from its more personalistic connotations and began to be used almost exclusively in the sense of "state".

201d853b-4474-51af-9e70-8502823535b6.definition: The 48th Chapter/Surah of the Quran, meaning "The Victory". It is composed of 29 verses.

b29a1eb8-4d03-527c-a470-6d9b2d53269c.definition: The 1st Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Opening". It is composed of 7 verses.

aaf61dd7-c338-5b59-9481-96b0fcd511b7.definition: A court official, equivalent to a chamberlain, which evolved to fulfil various functions, often serving as chief ministers or enjoying dictatorial powers.

a4191920-4704-5c00-a335-857aa8d5274e.definition: The 49th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Private Chambers". It is composed of 18 verses.

9c2e2004-3d90-5af9-823b-a7e2d698d965.definition: The 3rd Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Family of Irman". It is composed of 200 verses.

40da1488-6b0c-5407-91ab-fe344505219c.definition: The 18th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Cave". It is composed of 110 verses.

5da091ab-2521-5fd0-9c6b-804078feb293.definition: An honorific Islamic religious title given to Sunni Muslim religious scholars, generally means highly qualified Islamic scholar.

55aae703-bcda-5ede-aedc-b02a0583cc19.definition: The 67th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Sovereignty". It is composed of 30 verses.

9e9f2b8d-8a1b-5aca-ace2-23331cb7c2a6.definition: The 16th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Bees". It is composed of 128 verses.

b5507ca5-7b73-5ef6-a10a-9bc22a2496b2.definition: The 53rd Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Star". It is composed of 62 verses.

3d741e10-844b-53b3-bd76-b7ab36e8c586.definition: The 4th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Women". It is composed of 176 verses.

1dd45db8-f741-5e90-9598-aa5bed784e70.definition: The 54th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Moon". It is composed of 55 verses.

3242530f-aeca-5f8b-9d24-7679d72a87b6.definition: The 28th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Story". It is composed of 88 verses.

b6bf9297-6c19-524c-aaab-018a4692c5ad.definition: The 32nd Chapter/ Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Prostration". It is composed of 3- verses.

1732d847-9072-5d1d-8fac-f261ec1dcf98.definition: An Arab Muslim theologian, writer, and scholar, who was one of the first contributors of the principles of Islamic jurisprudence.

9e398194-c9e5-5b5c-ab78-4a4c9c5aea72.definition: Means "to send down". In Quranic terminology, it refers to the process by which divine message (the holy Quran) comes to the heart of the messenger.

df4c8625-0436-52ec-b25b-4c137d468556.definition: The 86th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Night Comer" or "The Night Star". It is composed of 17 verses.

782abace-0002-5e80-8b1f-a5cb1d7a353a.definition: The 9th Chapter/Sura of the Quran, meaning "The Repentance". It is composed of 129 verses.

081c777a-a6b8-599a-b2cc-1ea7f2513031.definition: Pottery jar for apothecaries’ ointments and dry drugs made in the Near East and in Spain and produced in Italy from the 15th through the 18th century. Since the jar had to be easy to hold, use, and shelve, its basic form was cylindrical but incurved for grasping and wide-mouthed for access.

16131753-740a-5b87-bfb9-06606e67de19.definition: A flag, banner or standard. They were carried next to a commander in a military campaign or were used in religious processions. They could be very different in shape and had geometric designs, sometimes with inscriptions. A metal *alem* could be mounted to the head of a pole.

0e59a881-b976-53f8-b105-4ec6f1ec35b6.definition: Alfardones (sg. alfardón) are elongated-hexagon tiles, usually decorated with text or floral and vegetative motifs.

39b15d5c-120b-51e4-b058-0cc18bb7226a.definition: From Ar. *farsh*. A flat ceiling of carved or artistically interlaced wood. It can also be a floor.

22b53494-49b4-56ac-8f6f-9b4231d55ce1.definition: (Pl. *alfices* (Es), *alfizes* (Pt)) From Ar. *hayyiz*. Rectangular surround to the Arabic arch, which frames the spandrels and starts from either the imposts or the base.

bd05e9dd-5e09-5d30-8a24-431c8cbf57da.definition: Ali Asghar, active around AD 977- 1008 / AD 1570-1600, was an artist in the Safavid court of Iran. He is particularly noteworthy for being the father of the renowned miniaturist Reza Abbasi, whose early artistic style likely bore the influence of Ali Asghar's work. Ali Asghar hailed from Kashan and, according to Qazi Ahmad, was one of Ahmad's teachers in the field of miniature painting. His career is believed to have commenced during the reign of Safavid Shah Tahmasp I (AH 930- 983 / AD 1524- 1576) before he relocated to Mashhad, where he emerged as one of the foremost painters in the service of the princely governor, Ibrahim Mirza, alongside other accomplished artists like Sheikh Mohammad and Abd-Allah.

b4b7cd95-2eef-5482-9f26-076ce3f742d8.definition: First letter of the Arabic alphabet.

d622d348-fe31-5163-9440-a84a07e7456c.definition: (Pl. *‘ulama’*) Scholar, doctor of law and Islamic theological science. Fr: ouléma or uléma. Tr: alim, pl. ulema.

e201e09c-f4b8-5f58-9289-a2b07a586749.definition: Angular polygonal decorative elements, formed in the shape of an almond. Along with other polygonal decorative elements, they are used in combination to make more elaborate and complex geometric decorative schemes.

c202ec3d-b7d3-5add-9412-a92b9475ea09.definition: So called "Pilgrim’s Companion". Gives advice to prospective pilgrims on every aspect of the journey.

46412584-c8d6-5149-bcf9-5194c433cdb9.definition: A movable star chart or map, also called rete. Ankabut also means spider in Arabic, which is also the name of the 29th chapter of the Quran.

128af9dc-bbcc-57e9-853d-989d596b41dc.definition: Nose septum ring, used as markers of ethnic identity and marital status among elderly Arabic women (in the settlement of Jeynav).

fb4643f3-3421-5aaa-8b4f-85806f394bac.definition: A designation for a two-dimensional ornamental pattern in Islamic art. Arabesques are constructed designs based on intertwined leaf stems and tendrils that create a continuous pattern sometimes in connection with scrolls or geometrical elements.

983e0813-bc71-581c-82c8-e8186f09992d.definition: A row of shops aligned along a street, which may be covered or open. See also *bazaar*, *bedesten*, *qaysariyya*, *suq*.

13b13347-73d9-5e9b-896e-e43453a70910.definition: (pl. of *rabat*). In Sufi tradition, an *arbita refers to a hospice combined with an educational establishment.*

4b276222-ccaa-52f9-9e53-a26c705c0197.definition: On the 10th day of Muharram, in Türkiye, both Sunni and Alevi-Bektashi Muslims prepare and share Ashura (also known as Noah’s pudding), a ritual dish believed to symbolise prosperity.

f80f3b72-49a9-5057-bd6f-021ba24a6071.definition: A medieval scientific instrument used for astronomical calculations and navigation.

1967d28e-68f6-5e68-b680-9a66e81477fb.definition: Commander-in-chief of the armies. Atabegs were appointed as tutors for young Seljuq princes acting as governors of important towns but they gained power and in time their independence.

7b9c0eb4-b88c-5f12-a29c-fb04001f136d.definition: From Ar. *tayfur*. Bowl or deep plate characteristic of al-Andalus ceramic production.

78fafab8-3f5e-5796-824d-1b42baff7c16.definition: From Ar. *tawriq*. Stylised plant motif ornamentation inspired by the classical acanthus, much used in Hispano-Muslim art.

6fd1696a-b5d7-52af-9ddf-69cb25fba143.definition: (Pl. *‘attarin*) Merchant of perfume, incense and medicinal plants.

6aa4c10c-2dae-5c27-8ba4-156ce70454d5.definition: Historic region of India (also called Oudh), since 1947 part of the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh

f8abb38d-e51e-5fc5-9493-dc1508482dcf.definition: Plural of Wakf, meaning religious endowments. Also meaning endowments.

8383edc1-0cb4-52fa-9e3a-219b3a940129.definition: (Pl. *ayat*) Verse in the Qur’an. Tr. ayet.

1a032c89-aa41-58cc-ab7b-69aae9ca6b91.definition: Verse number 255 from sura al-baqara, and it is known as "Master of the Noble Qur’an" because of its tremendous and countless favours and blessings in reading the ayat.

e6913e4d-77b8-54e6-8aff-ae3476396952.definition: Hexagonal decorative element. Along with other polygonal decorative elements, it is used to create more elaborate and complex decorative schemes.

b5ff90ab-5823-5d04-95e0-dc19f7472200.definition: A Spanish and Portuguese term for glazed tiles which have been set into a larger pattern to cover walls in courtyards of mosques and palaces. It is a term common all over the Maghreb. See also *zellij*.

def77096-6c70-5cc6-8614-c1a6edfaa358.definition: Ottoman artist. Although he did not produce ceramics himself, he is associated with the early phase of Ottoman ceramics from Iznik (late AH 9th / AD 15th century), which is called “Baba Naqqash ware”.

5414688b-b346-5448-a1fe-71b08489509c.definition: The Bahram Mirza Album is a collection of Safavid artworks compiled for Prince Bahram Mirza, who was the brother of Shah Tahmasp. This album was put together by Dust Muhammad between AH 950-51 / AD 1544-45.

6c6e93ba-0531-5a1f-bf45-acb1bac3ed4d.definition: A type of mantle, usually used to protect the head and shoulders from the sun.

e44ace71-d122-5c82-bf6b-34a79ff4b2d8.definition: Literally “sons of”, used to refer to members of a clan. Plural of *ibn / bin*.

ac67e975-1f75-526f-a8cd-402ccde93f6f.definition: A formula, *bi-‘ism Allah al-Rahman al-Rahim*, which is commonly translated as “In the name of God, the Clement, the Merciful”. Fr. *besmala*; Tr. *besmele*.

b8c40deb-d541-5941-870e-bbb5a22c7520.definition: (Pl. *biyut*) Room; in certain cases a house. *baytal-Hikma*: tribunal. *bayt ad-diwan*: reception hall. *bayt al-nar*: furnace, literally “house of the fire”. See also *dar*, *qasr*.

9f0f473b-d1c4-579a-830e-8c67cf9124bc.definition: Public market or designated place for commerce; covered market with doors (Persia). Fr. bazar. See also *arasta*, *bedesten*, *qaysariyya*, *suq*.

d262760a-d7c7-5583-b3d6-98f5a67ea709.definition: A commercial building with at least two aisles (in Istanbul three or four) and covered with domes of equal size. The most precious merchandise was kept in *bedesten*s, which functioned like banks do today. The word was derived from *bezzazistan* where bezzaz means a seller of fabrics. See also *arasta*, *bazaar*, *qaysariyya*, *suq*.

7aec7586-75a7-5362-b7c6-f62646540331.definition: A decorative technique developed in the AH 3rd / AD 9th century in Samarra for stucco panels, marble and woodwork, which shows vegetal ornaments in an abstract way and has slanted or bevelled contours.

816929a9-190c-57b7-8bc6-469a25050fac.definition: The ruler of an independent emirate; a title of respect for a man of the upper classes; title held by the sovereign vassals of the sultan. *Beylerbeyi*: The bey of beys: the highest rank in the provincial government of the Ottoman Empire. *Beylicat*, *beylik*: soverignty of or territory ruled by a bey. See also *agha*, *dey*.

5f340924-0a32-5b50-8c50-755492945fed.definition: In the Islamic world blue-and-white ceramics appeared in Mesopotamia in the AH 3rd / AD 9th century. Blue-and-white porcelain in China produced from the 8th / 14th century onwards had great influence in the Islamic world where it was collected at court and was imitated in the workshops of Ottoman Iznik and Safawid Iran.

73a9a2a0-a42b-53fb-aea6-1b24711d35fc.definition: A usually glass collar on a candle socket to catch drippings or on a candlestick or chandelier to hold suspended glass prisms.

53b06a4c-1741-53c4-bd23-415aa3ce7613.definition: Fort, bastion, tower, sometimes surrounded by an outer wall. The term passed into mediaeval Portuguese toponymy as *alvorge* or porches. In Tunisia it also means a secondary residence surrounded by gardens; a pleasure palace. Maghreb *borj*. Egypt *burg*. Tr. *burç*.

d27195f2-2e87-506e-8a8c-a4599a8d49cd.definition: A distintive felt hat somewhat like a stocking cap worn by Jannisaries.

5a9bc858-c027-5f9a-91c2-3756c4d27816.definition: A universal oriental rug design element. Boteh is Persian for "bush" and buta is Hindi for "flower".

f9464f31-431b-5219-aadf-e9d8a557c47a.definition: Term used to describe tiger stripe motifs.

66ada953-471d-537e-9767-a3228aab765c.definition: A charge in the shape of a solid diamond, rhombus, could also mean a bundle of cloths.

9a9a89fb-e90f-5cab-beec-84b022128bf3.definition: A burqa is a full body veil, and sometimes also refers to a part of the *kiswa*, the textile cover of the Ka’ba.

9c5b0b5e-062a-5b06-ace2-d6a40e4d5cb9.definition: The term "Bustaan" or "Bustan" directly translates to "Garden" or "Orchard." It is also the title of a poetry book penned by the Persian poet Saadi in AH 655/ AD 1257. The book is rich with valuable spiritual guidance and practical wisdom.

9e63c700-362b-5073-8fb1-689e160ff382.definition: A buzogan is most commonly interpreted as a mace, meaning it is a blunt weapon, usually made out of heavy material, particularly the head of the object.

b3b18f28-32c7-5836-ae64-e0df239443e1.definition: The Byzantine empire (306 to 1453) which was preceded by the Roman empire and succeeded by the Ottoman Empire.

b6c3a09c-964b-5dd3-a091-e608967fe6ff.definition: Ar. *khalifa* literally “successor”. The supreme head of the Muslim community. Caliphate: the territory under the power of the caliph.

c2953466-916b-57e9-9f3b-409c9af9afa1.definition: The “art of beautiful writing” (Greek) is one of the highest artforms of Islamic culture. As the Arabic language is connected with the revelation of Islam, calligraphy has deep spiritual undertones and is valued as a symbol of beauty and mystery. There are many types of calligraphy with variations according to period, place and context. Many artists of the Arab and Muslim world continue to practise calligraphy today. See also *diwani*, *farsi*, *kufic*, Maghribi-Andalusi, *muhaqqaq*, *naskhi*, *nasta’liq*, *rayhani*, *ruq’a*, *ta’liq*, *thuluth*.

014b74c8-3720-578e-b437-bd761597b51c.definition: Star shaped decorative element with five arms. Combined with other polygonal decorative elements, candilejos are used to make more elaborate and complex geometric decorative schemes.

801f574d-c2f6-52a3-ae7c-6a0074f1c59b.definition: From Persian. Hostel along main travelling routes to accommodate travellers and safeguard their goods. See also *funduq*, *khan*, *wikala*.

90c8aeb0-fee7-5ad8-b2e8-525f87d18e3a.definition: Fortress, citadel, usually equated with the city centre. Ar. *qasba*. *Ksiba*: small kasbah, the name of a neighbourhood in Bizerte, Tunisia. See also *hisn*, *qal’a*.

66c3c71a-cd8d-535b-aa60-f42837728e24.definition: A Latin term (pl. castra) meaning legionary camp, castle, fortified town.

a27048f2-e463-56af-bb14-17e5dd57b741.definition: A title of respect, given to men of the upper classes; the epithet of Sultan Mehmed I. Tr. *Çelebi*.

8013dd99-b044-5c32-9cd2-44d308c0c03d.definition: A term used in enamelled metalworking. Enamel glass powder is fired and fixed within depressions incised in the surface of the metal. In pottery this term is used for vessels with decoration standing out in relief obtained by taking away a slip and receiving an additional covering with a lead glaze.

988f73c6-aa80-5184-979f-cc026b118caf.definition: A frieze of geometric motifs, also meaning reminiscent of crenelations.

5a210dbc-4a3e-5d7f-b2d5-b9701b0f5a7c.definition: The chauri is a type of fan. It has a handle made of wood or metal. The rest is made of animal hair or nylon. When the Guru Granth Sahib is read, the granthi waves the chauri over the holy book from time to time.

e6ca4d52-63e1-5c91-8d45-5c007bd19735.definition: Artistic motifs originally from China that were used in Islamic art reflecting the strong Chinese influence since the Mongol periods. Typical designs are cloudbands, lotus-flowers and fabulous creatures such as the qilin. See also blue-and-white, *hatayi*, Ming-style, wave-and-rock motif.

4a4e8df2-25b4-5abc-8037-677cf2232c30.definition: A motif from Asia,  typical of Ottoman art of the AH 9th–11th / AD 15th–17th centuries and consisting of triple balls arranged in the form of a triangle together with double wavy lines thought to symbolise leopard spots and tiger stripes.

589d63b5-b3ff-5340-a217-d02452caa1bb.definition: Chogan is a traditional Iranian horse-riding game that incorporates music and storytelling, boasting a rich history of over 2,000 years in Iran. It was primarily enjoyed in royal courts and urban fields, with both men and women participated in the game.

cf4307ca-f437-5c58-80b8-f9b0100711fa.definition: A term used in enamelled metalwork. The enamel colours are laid in separate compartments as required by the design. These compartments are formed from thin metal strips set on edge so that the different colours cannot fuse during the firing process.

4a12c207-113d-5b87-992e-9db5d88374f3.definition: The first Muslim societies continued to use Byzantine solidus gold coins and Sassanian silver dirhams. In time, Qur'anic phrases, place of minting, names of caliph and sultan and Hijri date were added. With the Umayyad coinage revolution in AH 696–7 / AD 1296–7, pure epigraphic coins came into use. Akche: silver coin, basic unit of Ottoman money system; dinar: gold coin, equal to 10 dirhams; fils: copper coin.

a3daea50-dcf5-5a68-8ef1-532b1f81ebb3.definition: Woman’s court robe, characteristic for Romanian courts during the Ottoman period.

ecb796d7-8a47-5b6b-b1de-735827242cfc.definition:
"Corals, like pearls, are an organic material which have earned their place within the world of precious stones. They are valued not only for their physical properties and beauty, but also because of their symbolic and spiritual properties. Corals are miniature sea organisms called polyps, which live in warm and clear waters. Their skeletons consist mainly of calcium carbonate, which hardens after a coral dies. Coral colonies are made up of individual coral “trees” which, while growing, intertwine. Corals come in many colors, but the most common is red in a variety of shades.  
Corals are widely used for jewelry and other decorative arts. Many traits, positive and negative, have been attributed to corals, and they are mentioned in the histories of all cultures that had the opportunity to encounter them. The Quran briefly mentions corals, as well as rubies, as the stones that symbolize celestial women in paradise. In Hindu culture, it is believed that the tender young leaves of the Kalpa tree, a symbolical offering to the gods, were made of corals. In general, corals symbolize loyalty and sacrifice, and have also been associated with cures for the plague and other diseases. Belief in the healing powers of the stone has affiliated it with the protection of children."

44562f82-b0b6-5353-939a-47fccfb7fa3c.definition: Sacred text of the Islamic Revelation transmitted by the Archangel Gabriel to the Prophet Muhammad. From the root *qr*’, “to recite, to read”.

61dd2431-5d5a-563f-98ea-305257d3eed8.definition: Literally “dry cord”, a way of separating different coloured glazes on a tile during firing with greased cords. The term is also used for the technique of delineating the contours of a design with a mixture of wax or vegetable fat and manganese oxide. It is also known as “coloured glaze technique” in Turkish art and is seen in Turkey in the AH 9th–10th / AD 15th–16th centuries.

26c9c806-d472-53ee-82d8-4e2c5327925c.definition: Body armour that protects the torso above the waist or hips. It protected soldiers from direct sword, arrow or dagger hits during battle.

f3052f85-4db5-5572-a790-f3dc9a248659.definition: (Pl. *dur*) House. *Dar al-imara*: Governor’s house. Dar al-Islam: Domain of Islam: countries under Islamic rule; where Islam did not rule was considered war territory. *Dar al-Hadith*: A school for studying the Hadith; Tr. *Darülhadis*. *Dar al-Hijra*: Abode for migration. *Dar al-khuffaz*: A school for training of memorising the Qur’an; Tr. *Darülhuffaz*. Dar al-Qurra’: school for teaching Qur’an recitation as a science ; Tr. *Darülkurra*. *Dar al-shifa’*: hospital; Tr. *darüşşifa*. *Dar al-tibb*: A school where the medical sciences were taught; Tr. *Darüttıb*. See also *bayt*, *qasr*.

0b0c9320-1a31-574f-aa24-7c9a581717b2.definition: Alleyway, route. In Morocco and Tunisia derb: alley or by extension a neighbourhood. *Darb al-Hajj*: route taken to Mecca by pilgrims from every corner of the Islamic world. Usually all necessary services, especially security, were provided by the administration. Caravans would meet at specified times in designated places, e.g. the Turkish caravan would meet the caravan from al-Sham and they would travel together to join the Jordanian and Palestinian caravans.

b64a1f79-8f29-5ad4-8e98-379f8e05cb1b.definition: Member of a Muslim religious order noted for its devotional practices. Fr. *derviche*.

0c6702be-079c-5910-88ee-33a290820f45.definition: Holder of Sultan's ink bottle (from Persian دوات‌دار meaning bearer of the ink bottle), sometimes also referred to as secretary.

1a10a00e-64ff-5b66-8fec-3064ccfa26fe.definition: In decorative arts it usually refers to a decorative form, but it can also carry the meaning of vortex.

9e337d3c-af6d-5856-bb0c-0ed39eab0859.definition: Term used in Libya, Tunisia and Algeria for a high-ranking officer in the Turkish militia elected by a local council of janissaries. Below the Ottoman *Beylerbeyi* in rank deys nevertheless represented absolute power in the region. When they came into conflict with the Ottoman court, they were punished heavily. Tr. *dayı*. See also *agha*, *bey*.

31591fdd-18fb-5898-b2ac-33ccb03797c8.definition: A place with a very small population in the state and region of Amman Governorate in Jordan.

eb4ec166-81db-5b55-9f7c-de12b453b102.definition: The term dhikr comes from the triliteral root that means "to remember". In the context of the Islamic tradition, dhikr means the remembrance of God. This remembrance of God can take many forms. The word dhikr is also used to mean litanies and specific phrases in remembrance of God. This term could mean the Quran.

30a317f8-dd77-54b9-ba2d-fe25e643cf98.definition: A crown or headband, sometimes adorned with jewels. The word derives from the Greek *διάδημα* diádēma, "band" or "fillet",from *διαδέω* diadéō, "I bind round", or "I fasten".

a63b6fb1-4ed2-5e10-a649-69af7e23c299.definition: Diamonds (today) are known as the most prized gemstones, but they have not always had this reputation. They were primarily valued for their physical properties, particularly their hardness and fire resistance. Due to these traits, numerous myths have been created about diamonds, some of which date back to the 17th century or before. Several powers have been attributed to the stone, including purification, invincibility, and even the ability to spontaneously create others of its kind. In ancient Arabic medicine there was a belief that diamonds could cure all illnesses of the body and mind. One of the most popular legends involving diamonds is of the so-called Diamond Valley. Dating from the 4th century BC, the legend speaks of an inaccessible valley filled with snakes and other terrifying creatures, the floor of which is covered with an endless amount of diamonds. This legend has further contributed to the idea that diamonds are rare and immensely hard to find.

f68bb09f-0323-528e-a7bc-c97eec5531d8.definition: Monetary unit used in several countries. It was first introduced as an Islamic coinage in the late 7th century CE by Abd al-Malik of the Umayyad dynasty. The dinar dates from the Roman times, when it was known as denarius. Made of gold.

dc07b2ea-551e-5012-a166-43402ac5534c.definition: Silver coins, also used as a weight standard (2.97g).

90f70d34-04ee-5ee4-9a4d-560633a0eb6f.definition: A long usually white robe traditionally worn by men.

5117e6c8-5cec-5590-83a7-081569b2f889.definition: (demon, monster, fiend), often confused with *ḡūl (orge, ghoul) and jinn in both folk and literary traditions, expresses not only the idea of "demon", but also that of "ogre", "giant", and even "Satan". They are often black, with long teeth, black lips, blue eyes, claws on their hands, and large bodies covered with thick hair.*

3230cdd8-ec0e-5aa1-9b44-adc5716d86b8.definition: An office of government; audience hall, reception chamber; a collection of poems. Tr. divan; divan-ı Hümayun: the Imperial Council, chaired by the Grand Vizier, forming the central organ of the Ottoman government.

e1bb8c56-4a6a-520c-b924-22b130e433d1.definition: The divit is a Turkish/Persian calligrapher’s tool. The small side piece holds ink and the long part holds pens.

1f026bcb-0942-5877-8b20-c8bc0166a28b.definition: Central Asian antilope. The motif migrated via the trade routes to Northern China, and has become a common motif in embroidery, clothes, but also silverware. Chinese writers often identify the djeiran as a mythical rhinoceros that is said to gaze at the moon.

68be9f26-eb6e-5276-b60c-690997493d6e.definition: In military architecture the inner tower or stronghold of a castle, the keep.

a705554e-98ba-5dc4-9da0-a0510ecb2bd0.definition: A length of material worn arranged in two folds over the chest and thrown back around the shoulders.

1716f8d4-fa82-5204-b71c-843312201e82.definition: Central area in mosques and *madrasas*, giving access to other rooms. Usually surrounded by two or four *iwans*, and covered by a wooden ceiling with openings for light and ventilation.

c20c4a88-510d-575f-be26-b42955b12694.definition: Dust-Moḥammad was a highly regarded figure in the Indo-Persian realm, as well as among the Ottomans, due to his multifaceted talents encompassing painting, paper cutting, calligraphy tracing, and possibly bookbinding and gilding. He served as a secretary to Bahram Mirza, a notable Safavid prince who was both an art enthusiast and collector. Bahram Mirza acclaimed Dust-Moḥammad as the finest student of Behzad, a prominent artist of the time. It's important to note that Dust-Moḥammad should not be confused with another contemporary calligrapher by the same name, Dust-Moḥammad b. Solayman.

476a1ad7-f594-57bd-8ef5-ddfe4dba9e8b.definition: A lacquer technique first seen in Iran in the AH 9th / AD 15th century during the Timurid period. It was named after Edirne in Turkey from where the best examples came. It was used on different media such as bindings, drawers and bows.

16e5e640-a860-5917-bc5f-7e13a3825ded.definition:
"Emeralds are gemstones from the beryl mineral group which develop in a hexagonal shape. The gemstone got its name because of its color (from the Greek *Smaragdos*, meaning green stone), and it is said to symbolize the force of cosmic life, strength and inner peace.  
Emeralds are considered to be the gemstones of alchemists, who believe the emerald of wisdom gives life to nature. In Central America, they are related to fertility. In ancient Egypt, emeralds decorated funerary jewelry of noblemen and other high-ranking individuals. Because the gems were extremely rare, green colored glass or pottery were sometimes used instead."

8f750e3f-a3f4-5b39-8f9c-97cbf1eb56ec.definition: A military commander, prince or senior official; the ruler of an emirate or principality; Tr. *emir*. amir akhur: *amir* responsible for sultan’s stables, camels and postal service; Tr. *emir* *ahur* or imrahor. amir al-Mu’minin: Prince of Believers; Tr. *emirü’l-müminin*. amir al-Muslimin: Prince of Muslims; Tr. *emirü’l-müslimin*. amir al-silah: *amir* responsible for arms. amir kabir: Great Amir. Fr. *émir*.

5d77d3cf-d7dc-59de-8fe9-16b4846e152d.definition: Another name for slip, now largely obsolete.

f11aedf0-52d5-531a-89ae-fe60981d7a51.definition: Floor covering of a type apparently woven by all Turkmen tribes, with enough similarity in format to suggest that they are all descended from the same basic design. The field is usually quartered, with a thick band up the middle, at times culminating in an arch, as on the Tekke ensi.

cd62ef51-dfea-5e66-a924-b9ac8fd72a21.definition: A French term for maiolica, tin-glazed earthenware of post-Medieval Europe. Also a ceramic composed of a body of crushed quartz and an overlying glaze, common in the ancient Near East and Mediterranean. Capable of being moulded into small objects which were initially confused with earthenware with a white tin glaze and the term faience, incorrectly applied, has remained in use.

74e6afec-ff94-5208-be36-9ce20440d5ee.definition: A book of omens used by fortune tellers in Iran, India and Turkey during the 16th and 17th centuries. Individuals seeking insight into the future would engage in a series of purification rituals, turn to a random page in the Falnama, and interpret the text and drawings thereon for good or ill. Also known as divination books, they were also composed for rulers in need of guidance during military campaigns or who were caught in difficult political circumstances.

6f9e5b1d-8c35-59ba-9052-011f4c240ecf.definition: The evaluation of the goodness or badness of deeds according to the Islamic point of view was called *fiqh* (understanding), and the person holding the qualities of knowledge and competence to produce opinions in this respect was called faqih (the knowledgeable who understands well). The consideration of human actions within an Islamic religious context was encouraged by sayings of the Prophet, such as "He whom God favours with good, God makes him the one who understands in religion (*faqih*)".

3fd5d8e5-d6d9-5084-a7bc-f270946f8c24.definition:
"Farsi" refers to the Persian language. It is primarily spoken in Iran, Afghanistan, and Tajikistan and is written in the Persian script.  
  
1\. An inhabitant of Persia. 2. Cursive, particularly elegant calligraphic style which emphasises the curves of the Arabic letters by reducing the angular figures. See also calligraphy.

38f9b696-41fe-5bb6-aea9-f97476afeed6.definition:
This term has different meanings:  
  
Fez  
City in northern Morocco  
  
Fez  
A brimless cylindrical or somewhat cone-shaped hat with a flat top that usually has a tassel, is typically made of red felt, and is worn especially by men in eastern Mediterranean countries

664a6020-4914-5595-8215-d0a0af9a4b9e.definition: (Pl. *fuqaha’*) Muslim canonical jurisprudence. *Fqih*: jurisconsult versed in the code of Islam, the person specialising in *fiqh’*. There are four schools of Sunni legal schools of Orthodox Islam. See also Hanafi, Hanbali, Maliki, Shafi’i.

9710d010-10f2-5ad9-b13d-b664a92335eb.definition: A Persian poet who authored the Shahnameh. This monumental work stands as one of the most extensive epic poems ever composed by a single poet, and holds the esteemed position of being the preeminent epic within Persian-speaking nations.

111b1877-22ac-5026-90bf-a0267a993a00.definition: An edict of a sultan with official court directives. Firmans of the Ottoman sultans are paper scrolls of different length with an artistic signature (*tughra*) of the sultan as a heading, a written text in an official script followed by a number of testifying signatures at the end.

30b4ea5c-4774-5bfc-bea3-025184b06e0f.definition: A designation for a ceramic body consisting mainly of quartz and some glaze mixture. In the firing process the quartz and the glaze fuse to a white body, sometimes also called stonepaste.

720487c1-6546-5ad8-96ce-6caedac4ddab.definition: A leaf with illustration preceding the title-page of a book.

b54d5ba9-119e-5200-8993-1d307bd7f285.definition: A compendium of military arts written by Muhammad ibn ʿIsa ibn Ismaʿil al-Hanafi al-Aqsari, who dedicated it to the Mamluk viceroy of Egypt, Ala al-Din Asanbay al-Abu Bakri. It became the most popular Mamluk book on *furusiyya (horsemanship) and many illustrated copied were made for Mamluk patrons in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries.*

0608107a-ec5a-529b-8814-e74d5f7ea1bd.definition: A traditional outer garment worn in Iran during the Qajar period.

ac65deea-d395-59f6-bb9f-0cdc678424a3.definition:
"The term garnet includes a large group of silicate minerals which have the same basic structure and a consistent chemical formation which occasionally vaires when other elements are present. The name of this gemstone derives from the Latin term *granum*, meaning grain. Garnets come in all colors, among which the most common is red and the rarest is blue. Garnets can be divided into a series of subtypes: pyrope, almandine, spessartine, grossular, uvarovite and andradite.  
The most popular and widely used of these is the pyrope subtype. For a long time, pyropes and almandines were grouped under the same name, which was carbuncle. In ancient Judeo-Christian legend, it is believed that Noah used a carbuncle to light up his arc. The name pyrope comes from the Greek word *pyropos*, meaning fire-like, since pyropes are of a recognizable red palette. The stone was particularly popular around the globe in the 18th and 19th centuries. The main sources of this subtype of garnet can be found in the Czech Republic, which is why it was commonly called the “Czech Ruby”. Because of their abundance, garnets are omnipresent in European decorative arts. Garnet mines can also be found across Europe, Southeast Asia, and Africa."

526a9319-af7c-51c1-a368-2df37f43ebcf.definition: Water pipe, commonly used for tobacco smoking.

d0a5c7c0-4aea-55a1-99af-300a6e2be808.definition: A type of knife. Could also refer to the ubiquitous short lyric whose cultivated formal rhetoric readily allows its expressions of private feeling to achieve widespread public outreach through recitation and musical performance as well as written dissemination. Also, could refer to a gazelle.

1123d155-1d0c-59e5-8ecc-ca1e2b7a31e9.definition: From ghazwa (military raid), referring to a noble title for those who participated in battles for Islam. It became a military rank during the Mamluk period and was notably applied to Mahmud of Ghazni, as inscribed on Mahmud’s Tower in Ghazni in AH 421 / AD 1030. Tr. *gazi*.

09e9e553-3757-50e9-a411-6aaea263cdac.definition: The so-called Turkish knot in a pile rug or carpet. Another term is symmetrical knot or double knot. The asymmetrical knot exists in Persian carpets, called a Senneh knot.

e0e8a76f-5937-523a-b87b-6d2a0c6528d7.definition: Applying gold to the surface of an artwork. Gilding can be applied to most materials, including marble, stone, stucco, wood, metalwork, ceramics, glass and paper. Different techniques are used to apply gold, as it can be applied in a light wash or as gold-leaf foil. Tr. *tombak*, gilded copper technique.

f2b2bdf4-e6b8-5c67-94e3-3fdbc00d8e88.definition: A thin layer of glass is applied to the surface of a ceramic before firing. In the kiln firing the glaze fuses, protecting the ceramic and making it waterproof and suitable for different purposes. Lead glaze is transparent and soft but vulnerable to cracking and chemical deformation. Tin glaze: an opaque white glaze containing tin, developed in Baghdad in the AH 3rd / AD 9th century to rival Chinese porcelain and transmitted from there to Moorish Spain and then the rest of Europe. Faience, maiolica and Delft wares have tin glazing.

04723e93-e903-5ff8-abd0-54ec24fd67cf.definition: Italian, literally, “scratched”. The pottery vessels made in this technique have received a slip and a decoration that is incised through the slip showing the contrasting colour of the body. The decoration is then covered with an additional lead glaze.

bf45b8ed-e1ac-5ab7-a72d-85c57ebcf786.definition: A decorative ceramic glazing technique where the only colours used are the green of copper oxide and almost black manganese. At the end of the process, the whole composition is covered with a transparent layer of lead glaze.

3c9bbe16-2c54-5e14-a88a-57b9fca326d5.definition: Literally means flower or rose in Turkish but could also refer to a large octagonal design derived from the shape of a rose, a motif on Oriental rugs.

ed99231a-c0b2-5d20-a744-24e1dda99d0d.definition: Literally meaning rose garden. It also refers to a literary work, a book of Persian prose written in 1258 by Sheikh Sadi Shirazi, a writer widely recognized as one of the greatest masters of the classical Persian literary tradition.

2fb79a2a-639b-5703-9b25-ab627b16aef8.definition: A gift of real estate bequeathed in perpetuity under certain conditions in favour of a mosque or other religious institution, such as a *madrasa* or *khanqah*, or a civil institution such as a *sabil*, or even a house. See also *waqf*.

c18561f3-9ed2-5c21-92a7-c3476d781d57.definition: Literally, “sayings”. Body of traditions related to the sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad and his companions. *Dar al-Hadith*: see *dar*.

34de20aa-0e07-573b-bdd7-f5b965cda195.definition: "Seven Thrones," known in Persian as "Haft Awrang," is a renowned work of Persian literature by the poet Jami, believed to have been written between AH 872- 890 / AD 1468 and 1485.

78fbda06-59a1-5c53-968c-a29d97e17693.definition: Haft rang is a type of decorative ceramic tile that is famous for its vibrant and colourful designs. Haft Rang Tiles have a long history, dating back to ancient Persia (modern-day Iran). They have been used for centuries to decorate architectural structures, palaces, mosques, and other important buildings. Becasue of this, these tiles are considered a significant part of both Persian and Islamic art and architecture.

15a4f195-ae31-5896-b05c-fd48066bbab1.definition: In Persian literally “seven colours”. A polychrome glazing technique used in Persia in the Middle Ages, in which the pigments developed into brilliant colours under an alkaline glaze after a second firing.

2321357b-4aa3-502a-a078-82ed79384c60.definition: Female garment worn in Algeria particularly in central Algeria. Also describes the word for embroider.

4a7c27f5-2059-522b-a21e-ee99a0c6ac00.definition: A high government official. The term originally designated a chamberlain, but under the Spanish Umayyads the *hajib* functioned as a chief minister, paralleling the position of vizier in the eastern caliphates.

cccf5396-0f64-5785-9f34-bb8b7a5ffd5b.definition: One of the five pillars of Islam: pilgrimage to Mecca and holy places, which all believers must accomplish at least once during their lifetime if they have the means to do so. By extension it also refers to someone who undertakes the pilgrimage. Hajj takes place two months after Ramadan and finishes with the Feast of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha). ‘Umra has almost the same rituals as the Hajj but takes place outside the Hajj season. ‘Umra’s significance is growing because there is no means to house the increasingly large numbers (over three million) who want to go on Hajj.

de7e96f7-ca25-58f9-a626-c8701ca41269.definition: "Halnameh," or "Guy u Chugan," is a mystical masnavi by Mahmud ibn Muhammad Aarifi Heravi, a poet and mystic of the Timurid era.

22b364bf-65ea-5573-8c73-2d90f70153fc.definition: The name Muhammad is derived from the Arabic root word hamada, meaning "praise", and can be translated as the "Oft - praised One". Could also refer to fertile land.

7357d832-1e4b-5e25-ae5c-44e119c49d9f.definition: Hamadan, historically known as Ecbatana/ , is a city in western Iran and the capital of the Hamadan Province. Renowned for its historical significance, it is one of the oldest continually inhabited cities in the world. Hamadan has a rich cultural heritage, with landmarks such as the Ganj Nameh inscriptions and is home to many notable tombs, including those of Esther and Mordechai. The city has played a pivotal role throughout various periods in Iranian history and offers a blend of historical sites and traditional markets giving it a vibrant atmosphere.

fc74d5ab-7517-53a5-9a58-0cb34c65fec8.definition: Public or private bathhouse. Apodyterium: changing room; Tr. *soyunmalık*. Caldarium: hot room. Hypocaust: floor and wall heating system by steam in Roman baths and villas. Tepidarium: warm room where bathers would rest after bathing; Tr. *ılıklık*. Also in Turkish bathhouse: *aralık*: passageway between the *soyunmalık* and *ılıklık*; *halvet*: private chambers in a public bath; *traşlık*: small room used for the removal of body hair. Also in Syrian bathhouse: *barrani* (lit. “exterior”): the cold room of a bathhouse because it is usually located furthest from the furnace; *juwwani*: most interior part, closest to furnace – steam room; *wustani*: middle chambers designated as the “warm water chambers”. See also *maqsura*.

cc92b83e-cb72-55df-b6de-8ddaf5a44e3f.definition: One of the four Sunni legal schools of Orthodox Islam. Tr. Hanbeli. See also *fiqh’*.

982c3a21-b99b-5c3b-b3d3-65276466c18d.definition: One of the four Sunni legal schools of Orthodox Islam. Founded by Abu Hanifa al-Nu‘man, it became the chosen school of the Ottomans. Tr. Hanefi. See also *fiqh’*.

98126354-fd6d-514c-b8f3-e1e9c98539e5.definition: Sacred plant and the drink made from it. Haoma is also personified as a divinity. It bestows essential vital qualities—health, fertility, husbands for maidens, even immortality.

d71360cd-eac1-5408-b6b3-59ad3d8464b9.definition: Ar. literally “sacred”, “forbidden”. Sanctuary. An illicit act from the religious point of view. Haram al-Sharif: the Noble Sanctuary in Jerusalem including al-Aqsa Mosque and Dome of the Rock.

0ad8de69-3a63-53bc-8e1b-4c6cae853bca.definition: Common living space in a Turkish house. Tr. also *sofa*.

e66e69a5-bb8f-5155-9d62-63d9729f3cfa.definition: Type of Persian rug. Instead of originating from a specific area, these rugs are categorized by their designs and patterns. The designs used in the Herati rugs are labelled as Herati as well, hence where the name originates.

16851f92-8fb5-54ee-8fd1-58ab8dc1b8f5.definition: The collective name for a number of early Arabic scripts that developed in the Hejaz region of the Arabian Peninsula, which includes the cities of Mecca and Medina.

0f3fb66d-a491-591b-a0c2-56e11ec481aa.definition: Muhammad’s flight from Mecca to Madina in AD 622. The beginning of the Muslim Hijri (Hegira) calendar, which follows a lunar year.

c0013a33-832b-5aec-b97e-3901d8475a95.definition: The crescent Moon, also known as the most common symbol of Islam.

dcd58376-8ba5-5488-bec0-53d4cf2fa497.definition: A prose description of the Prophet Muhammad. Hilya-i Sharif: noble description of the prophet, a work of art bearing the noble description.

30791f6d-6352-5d7a-8002-6f4f250bd3c4.definition: Necklace, could also refer to an amulet.

07f9ade5-1099-54b3-9064-0e9a6525cda8.definition: A seat or covered pavilion on the back of an elephant or camel.

c8f1dda2-4eb6-56a9-ab2a-90bd17c5301c.definition: The 11th sura of the Quran, it has 123 verses (ayat). It relates in part to the prophet Hud.

20ec2a87-3b3c-5cbe-94d3-205645c7a199.definition: A pipe traditionally used for smoking flavoured tobacco in which tobacco is placed in a bowl and heated with burning charcoal, producing smoke that is drawn through an urn of water that cools it and then into a long tube with an attached mouthpiece.

f02daf1a-8cf3-537e-9527-27663513c0ba.definition: The term Huri refers to a beautiful maiden who awaits the devout Muslim in paradise. The Arabic word *ḥawrāʾ signifies the contrast of the clear white of the eye to the blackness of the iris. There are numerous references to the houri in the Qurʾān describing them as 'purified wives' and 'spotless virgins'.*

c58452c8-0bf7-5a14-8773-673ad0923590.definition:
Unfortunately, no information has been found about his life in contemporary sources, and further investigation is required. However, below is information about some artworks attributed to him:  
The Mausoleum of Imamzadeh Qasim, known as the Astana Mausoleum, is situated in the centre of the city of Babol. Its entrance, the creation of Husayn ibn Master Ahmad Saravi, features a beautiful and intricately carved door, dating back to the year AH 890 / AD 1485. Within the mausoleum, an elegant, exquisitely carved box sits atop Imamzadeh's grave. Constructed during the month of Sha'ban al-Mo3azam in the year AH 888 / AD 1483, as with the entrance way, this box is also the craftsmanship of Husayn ibn Master Ahmad Saravi.

d741661c-846f-560d-a11c-19720819ac9a.definition: Son of, used in names. To indicate a clan the plural form *Bani / Banu*. is used. Tr. –*oğlu*.

1cde97a5-238a-57b7-ae98-c6e06d4dd4a2.definition: A small metal pot, usually of copper, with a long metal handle, used for preparing Turkish, Arabic, or Greek style coffee. Could also refer to a spouted jug made of metal or clay, usually used for ablution.

2fd97666-d841-5836-9a30-b7ba1b844921.definition: A buckle for belts, usually made of precious metals, especially silver.

3dc337fc-c4b3-5090-8e5a-a4545babb59a.definition: Belt worn by a male pilgrim and used for carrying valuables while performing the Hajj rites, also donates a state of mind in which a Muslim must enter in order to embark on Hajj. Also refers to the unsewn textile outfit worn by pilgrims.

87122e5b-a77c-5347-b610-ee9b8c2fd3ca.definition: A form of educational certificate. The ijaza could take different forms: it could be a formal attestation of a scholar that some individual had, in some fashion, studied a particular text with him, or it could be his statement that the student had mastered an entire field of learning. In any case, it was a personal document, which confirmed the relationship of the student to his teacher, and through him to his teacher’s own instructors. Through it, the student took his place in a genealogy of authorities that constituted the only recognized hierarchy of the educational system at the time.

de12acd8-39dd-5dba-ac9c-b6e91df924c7.definition: Ikat fabric is a dyeing technique used to create a distinct style of textile patterns. Ikat is done by resist dyeing sections of the yarns prior to weaving the fabric.

78382734-788f-5068-b99e-3cc129b1f007.definition: Political entity officially known as Iranzamin. It was established and ruled by the Mongol House of Hulagu.

441e3156-be30-517c-a195-12e2d3486ed8.definition: One who presides over Islamic prayers, a guide, chief, spiritual model or cleric; sometimes also a political leader in Muslim society.

8f367dab-0120-518e-b2ab-f888fb65bc16.definition: Office or region and country ruled by an Imam (spiritual leader).

0b81a7a9-57fd-5a5c-b6f0-f67773236be6.definition: Imam refers to a holy person in Shia Islam. Imamzadeh refers to their offspring.

7fb96b21-abb1-5f60-883e-2d6e33ce522d.definition: This is a term in Swahili meaning flourishing, strong.

d92f6fd0-31e4-5a3e-a04f-1708743e899b.definition: From Ar. *imara*. A complex of buildings and institutions supported by a *waqf*. After the AH 10th / AD 16th century a public soup-kitchen for the poor.

e6385177-2664-5111-8f62-1320456abb8d.definition: Rectangular basin in the centre of an atrium in the open air for the collection of rainwater.

471e3135-0bfb-5648-b37a-608939ef3fed.definition: Arabic name for the Gospel of Jesus (*Isa*), or any gospel in general. It is usually spelled *injil*.

a23158c9-7afc-5a3c-ad75-9ecc73727c13.definition: A technique in which cut ivory, mother-of-pearl, tortoiseshell or the like are arranged in a geometrical pattern, often within a wooden framework.

96a108d1-019f-555a-b601-5b20e5a11257.definition: Land given to army officers in exchange for military and administrative duties.

ffd69886-00a2-5968-b0e0-16249a1412eb.definition: A cultural and historical treasure in central Iran, often referred to as "Nesf-e Jahan" (Half of the World) due to its grandeur and beauty. Isfahan is famous for its stunning architecture, including the Imam Mosque, Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque, and the historic Naqsh-e Jahan Square. It has a rich history as a capital of the Persian Empire during the Safavid dynasty and is renown for its Persian handicrafts and exquisite tilework.

1bcff5a5-1586-5d9e-a84e-b16a4a88bdae.definition: The Prophet Muhammad’s midnight journey from Mecca to Jerusalem.

ed1392a3-c2e4-5dca-8b74-eaef4f0f9c94.definition: A vaulted hall or domed hall, walled on three sides with a large opening arch. Tr. eyvan.

eb5afced-0046-5fd2-aa51-8192d7a0f140.definition: Fragment of lintel, a textile outfit.

0c7c1002-ee4f-5507-9e43-3d8636035b0a.definition: A type of architectural decoration, usually in the form of a window grill, constructed of ornaments, geometric motifs and other shapes.

273dff1e-b908-5770-9385-d987f829c77f.definition:
"The term jade refers to two types of minerals: jadeite, which is a silicate of sodium and aluminium; and nephrite, a silicate of magnesium, potassium and iron. The two types are quite difficult to distinguish from one another, and therefore are both commonly called jade. These minerals both measure at six point five to seven on the Mohs scale. When cut, jade has a matte appearance, but possesses extraordinary shininess when polished. It comes in a variety of colors, among which the most prized are green, pink and yellow.  
The presence of jade in human history dates back over seven thousand years, and in myths it is one of the most mystical and mysterious gemstones. Cultures from many regions, such as South America, Asia and the Pacific Islands, all have their own versions of the story of how jade got its name. Jade is a very important gem in Chinese culture, appearing in many shapes and forms, and is affiliated with numerous beliefs of both protective and romantic natures. It is also believed that when struck, jade can produce the sound of a loved one’s voice. Talismans made from this precious stone are also popular in the Islamic world, especially among ethnic Turks, who pass them through generations as heirlooms."

96a4f75a-c342-596d-869f-1064cf498d88.definition: A period of ignorance, referring to the paganism of pre-Islamic Arabia. Tr. Cahiliye.

67598158-abd4-5f84-bfbe-7e8aef285bdf.definition: A traditional Arab garment worn by both males and females. It predates Islam and is worn over other clothing. The female version may be elaborately adorned and includes a head covering. The male version, a simple robe, is also variously called thawb, thobe and dishdasha (in the Levant) and Kandura in the United Arabic Emirates. The details of the garment - sleeve length, distance from the floor etc may vary.

070e713b-f503-5f87-be41-16cb73c070b4.definition: Main mosque where daily prayers and Friday prayers are celebrated. Tr. *cami*. See also *meşrebiye*.

b1ec8e21-3e6a-5dda-9949-a516128c3408.definition: An officer in the army of India, or any of several police or other officials of the government of India.

7910cc31-4aef-536d-b917-919e64b075ff.definition: The Ottoman sultan’s standing infantry corps, recruited from non-Muslims under the devşirme system and paid from the Treasury. Tr. *Yeniçeri Ocağı*.

98c1ae85-7402-57f8-8697-ad40faeafd69.definition: A type of intricately joined wooden ceiling in which supplementary laths are interlaces into the rafters supporting the roof to form decorative geometric patterns. This term is Moroccan, but it also has a Spanish term – *artesonado*.

90bd1da2-abb0-5d9c-b340-7fc034249c2e.definition: Striving towards moral and religious perfection, the motivation for which may lead to fighting “on the path to God” against dissidents or pagans.

9b746350-d82d-5ab5-9676-62bdb3be99b1.definition: View of the World', a geographical work written by Kâtip Çelebi (Turkish historian, geographer, and bibliographer) that makes the first use, in Turkey, of European atlases and other sources.

f3e0634c-24ec-55cb-977b-33628dad645e.definition: A type of sword. The jineta sword is most well-known like hispanoarabe, used by the Muslims in the peninsula from 13th century, later the jineta sword was made and used by the Christians from the 15th century.

b3d75c6a-1878-50e5-88da-5dc169dc75c0.definition: A spirit inhabiting the earth but unseen by humans, capable of assuming various forms and exercising extraordinary powers. Belief in jinn was common in pre-Islamic Arabia, where they were thought to inspire poets and soothsayers. Their existence was affirmed in the Qurʾān, and they are conceptualized in Islam as creatures parallel to human beings who are capable of choosing between good and evil and must thus face eventual salvation or damnation. They are beings of smokeless flame by nature, in the same manner in which humans are said to be made of earth, and they cannot be seen by human beings.

3b8250d6-be83-56b0-b0c6-75e45abdb1e7.definition: The only way a non-Muslim territory could avert a war with the abode of Islam was either to convert to Islam or to pay an annual poll tax (*jizya*) and thereby accept the hegemony of the Islamic caliphate.

41bd67aa-d50c-5f48-99eb-3debc6dce503.definition: Captain of the polo team/polo player.

2003ec95-a720-51cb-9dcd-774d9dc9f389.definition: The text of the Qur’an can be divided into 30 equal sections. One-thirtieth is therefore called a *juz’* (pl. ajza). When Qur’ans were written in 30 volumes, as in Mamluk Egypt, one volume was a *juz’*.

98afafd6-f8b6-5d37-923e-752f4697a5a7.definition: Literally “cube”. Temple in Mecca, the centre of the Islamic religion.

c4bd090a-f131-5065-9dbe-2761690061ca.definition: Limestone used in paving and in the frames of doors and windows.

dde3bab2-6c93-59de-b512-d4ebe4ea584d.definition: A usually cotton or silk ankle-length garment with long sleeves that is common throughout the Islamic world.

a440e09c-19a4-5c75-a54b-ddacd997f4c6.definition: Colourful decoration done with a k*alem* (brush) on a plastered surface.

a5dc60b2-f250-5e30-b242-9a7e914f186d.definition: Meaning knife and could also refer to a craftsman who makes knifes or qalams.

76f6a9f3-621f-5627-9ea8-42831078a1f9.definition: Behzad was a prominent Persian artist who held leadership positions in the royal workshops of Herat and Tabriz during the late Timurid and early Safavid eras. He is renowned for representing the pinnacle of excellence in the esteemed tradition of Islamic miniature painting. Behzad's birth is estimated to have been around AH 859 / AD 1455 in Herat, Khorasan, and he is believed to have passed away in approximately AH 942 / AD 1536 in Tabriz, Azerbaijan.

af45fe93-c833-5d32-b513-69ff4815f5ba.definition: A broad waist sash, usually pleated, which is often worn with single-breasted dinner jackets.

7640516c-0c76-5b6f-a9de-f1ab4b92ab78.definition: A straight, single-edged dagger that is worn on the left side of the belt.

a69e0be4-5747-5dbc-a7a3-cd85630b3c1d.definition: Type of tile. The word kashi (tile) has derived from the name of Kashan City which has been well-known as the center of tile making and pottery industry since the early Islamic period.

0e06d30a-be13-5433-806d-bc31ca55617d.definition: A type of push dagger from the Indian subcontinent. The weapon is characterized by its H-shaped horizontal hand grip which results in the blade sitting above the user's knuckles.

ba012528-e332-58db-968d-165b78bc6d94.definition:
A kilim is a traditionally crafted flat tapestry-woven carpet or rug originating from countries that were part of the former Persian Empire, such as Iran, the Balkans, and Turkic nations.  
Kilim is woven from silk, goat hair, sheep's wool, or other domestic quadrupeds.

ec2ffb6d-71b9-507b-8f5b-d77c262a8f40.definition: A name used for various types of stringed bowed musical instruments originating in the Eastern Mediterranean, particularly in Armenia, Greece, Iran, Turkey, and Azerbaijan, and regions adjacent to the Black Sea. These instruments are folk instruments, generally having three strings and played held upright with their tail on the knee of the musician.

1a551412-ba3d-5a82-89e6-07e97018fb70.definition: Brocade, a multi-coloured Ottoman compound-woven fabric using polychrome silk with gold, gilded silver and silver metallic threads to achieve colourful designs.

04f42d3e-3607-5497-ac48-4aa51fe765d3.definition: A small room or cell (sometimes an independent building) with few or no windows to which Sufis retreat. It corresponds to the *halvet* of a Turkish bath – see *hammam*.

5805ea4d-515f-570c-944e-b39504e35c2a.definition:
This term has two meanings:  
  
HAND OF FATIMA  
The “Hand of Fatima” or “Khamsa”, which can be found in souks all around Morocco, be it metallic, ceramic, coloured or made from camel bone, is a very widespread talisman. Khamsa means “five” and refers to the five fingers of the hand. Khamsa is an amulet which is typical of both the Islamic and Jewish religion.  
  
QUINTET OF POEMS  
"Khamsa" typically refers to the quintet of poems composed by the Persian poet Nezami Ganjavi in the 12th century. This collection, recognized as the "Khamsa," which means five in Persian and Arabic, or "Quintet," the term used in Europe, comprises five epic poems)," “Makhzan al-Asrar” ( The Treasury of Mysteries), "Khosrow and Shirin," "The Seven Beauties," "Eskandar-Nameh" (The Book of Alexander), and "Layla and Majnun." "Khamsa" is a compilation of Mathnawi poems, employing rhyming couplets, a specific form of Persian poetry well-suited for longer narrative works. Nezami's "Khamsa" is esteemed for its poetic beauty, moral depth, and the adept interweaving of historical and mythical elements. This masterpiece has left an enduring impact on Persian literature, being actively studied and appreciated for its literary and cultural significance.

cf7d3667-7d96-58e6-af31-c5d6fe2c71b8.definition: Ar. Inn, lodgings on the main caravan routes for travellers (pilgrims and merchants) and where merchandise could be stored. See also *caravanserai*, *funduq*, *wikala*. Tr. *han*.

1863aa1c-4cad-53d2-a497-ecb16318e81f.definition: Monastery or hostel for itinerant Sufis or dervishes. Tr. *hanikah*, *hankah*. See also *zawiya*.

c6e9e6d3-1a7c-5bc2-bf75-31b1070e8288.definition: One of the Persian arts of marquetry wherein the surface of wooden or metallic articles is decorated with pieces of wood, bone and metal cut in a variety of shapes and designs.

069e3a86-9304-50ec-85c5-b13302126d14.definition: An Arabised version of the Turkish *Hatun*, a title of respect for women of the upper classes.

364dd964-3408-5e4e-8db6-c9b7e5e3d30a.definition: Egyptian art of tent-making is created using a hand-applique technique in which fabric pieces are cut, folded and skilfully hand-sewn to canvas, producing impressive tents and wall hangings. These vibrant textiles are widely used in ceremonial contexts such as weddings, funerals, street parties and religious events.

6dc0bc86-bae7-595d-afd4-5801f58f6005.definition: Treasurer, responsible for State coffers (khaza’in) where the money and gold of the sultan or *amir* was kept.

b8b82127-2aac-57e8-ba1a-3104f9b6f7a3.definition: Word used to describe a library, but could also mean closet, depending on the dialect and context.

2a3c0ddd-2061-5547-b807-78d7dfc8a700.definition: A vast historical region in north-eastern Iran, known for its diverse culture and history. It encompasses several major urban centres, including Mashhad, the holiest city in Iran due to it being home to the Imam Reza Shrine. Khurasan has been a centre of trade, scholarship, and civilization for centuries, with influences from various dynasties and empires.

aace2213-b96e-55dc-90b1-8852a726d654.definition: The weekly sermon of the Friday prayer. Tr. *hutbe*.

c7a6e5ba-2a85-5491-b7e4-4bdb152f4a22.definition: A historically significant city and province located in south-eastern Iran. Kerman is renowned for its rich cultural heritage, including traditional crafts like carpet weaving, as well as its architectural marvels such as the Ganjali Khan Complex and the Jameh Mosque. The region is known for its desert landscapes, particularly the Lut Desert, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Kerman is also celebrated for its unique cuisine, blending Persian and Baluchi flavours, and its pivotal role as a hub on the historic Silk Road, fostering trade and cultural exchange between the East and the West.

53d47884-ba36-5979-a58f-ff35b0bd8587.definition: A cloth composed of different parts to cover the Ka’ba in Mecca. It is embroidered in silk and gold with Qur’anic verses. A new one is made each year. The change takes places during the Hajj, when the old *kiswa* is cut up and distributed among the people. Cloths with zigzag patterns of calligraphy that cover mausolea cenotaphs are also called *kiswa* (e.g. in Palestine).

a2cd2122-5bfb-5529-969c-e354791fd4c1.definition: Curved single-edged Sword with Kattara Hilt.

c165399e-b08f-5181-841f-72a17449e691.definition: Persian ceramic ware, painted in a free expressive style and covered with cracks. This conventional name came from a village in Daghestan, where in the 19th century huge amounts of Iranian Safavid pottery were concentrated.

493375fc-3554-5e13-aecc-2cf8ffc093d8.definition: Term used to describe a dome.

5680e113-6b9f-5043-82ac-d9da92afcd18.definition: Leather case, could also refer to a grave.

95fc5a14-1b29-5364-810a-69fc76087256.definition:
An Arabic script of angular and stylised characters used in Qur’ans in the early period of Islam. It is attributed to the city of Kufa in Iraq. From the AH 4th / AD 10th century it was less used because it could be difficult to read. Foliated *kufic*: a script that combines the angular style of the letters with decorative floral and vegetal motifs as finials, popular during the Fatimid and Atabeg period. See also calligraphy.  
  
Kufic script emerged as an Arabic script style, initially rising to prominence as the favoured choice for transcribing the Qurʾan and adorning architectural structures. Over time, it evolved into a point of reference and an exemplary model for various other Arabic scripts. Kufic script is characterised by its markedly angular form within the Arabic alphabet, originating in the initial copies of the Qurʾan.

a4d6e710-9d7b-5677-86d7-f2c2f3603a39.definition: Also known as the Andalusian "ʿud" (i.e., lute), the kuitra is a lute variant mostly found in North Africa.

81dc2164-deae-5d1f-8a05-4e038d6354b1.definition: An Ottoman Turkish term that refers to religious and charitable complexes comprising several buildings with the mosque is at the centre. The other buildings were the hospital, bathhouse, soup-kitchen *darüşşifa* (hospital), *hammam* (bathhouse), *han* (lodgings), *imaret* (soup-kitchen), *madrasa* (school).

efe31d1d-66e8-5909-b11e-f8bc1f80884a.definition: A form of jewellery made from gold, usually with a core of wax. The term kundan itself means highly refined pure gold, and this type of jewellery generally involves 24k pure gold.

a931a38f-be76-52dd-a8c8-ba68d6149d1c.definition: A technique used in Turkish-Islamic woodwork using specially designed pieces of wood that can be interlocked with adjoining pieces without using glue or nails to make a complete pattern. The technique is used for different woodworks, such as doors or shutters. In fake *kündekari* the parts are glued or nailed onto a surface.

6d80067a-11d1-5a05-8e27-1c1e30ff12b0.definition: Word used for chair or throne, depending on the context.

db724d75-473e-54fa-80e2-dc1b1779e4d7.definition: A sort of multicoloured head band or hairband.

747c42e9-649d-5559-a7b6-1d32a0a36949.definition: A ceramic technique (from Persian *lajvard*, – lapis lazuli) in which a monochrome coloured glaze was applied to a tile or vessel, which was then fired. The ceramic was then painted with an enamel colour and fired a second time. Like lustreware, *lajvard*ina wares were costly to produce and are only found in Ilkhanid Iran.

961fe836-4b40-5496-978f-d23cca1475bd.definition: A ceramic technique in which raised or incised lines separate the different colours of a painted vessel in order to keep them from fusing. This type of pottery was made in Syria and Iran in the AH 6th / AD 12th century.

5caf2c52-a5b1-520d-aa0a-f9f2d56b13ec.definition: Term used to describe a necklace.

642f2ce2-807c-5e5a-b4f5-d6f4bbb30fbb.definition: Literally means board in Turkish, but also refers to calligraphic panels.

04388740-935d-5fa5-a46c-62f30988a4ad.definition: The Lion and Sun, denoted in Persian as "Shir o Xorsid," stands as a significant emblem within Iran (formerly Persia). It was a prominent element of Iran's national flag until the AH 1399 / AD 1979 revolution. Illustrating a blend of traditions, it features a lion looking to its left, holding a sword in one paw with the rays of the sun shining behind it. Its origins can be traced to an ancient astrological sign associated with the sun's presence in the house of Leo- an emblematic representation of power and royal authority.

979bdd19-30d6-5bb0-bcfa-de1a9378304f.definition: Liqa refers to a type of textile. Liqa also refers threads of silk which are used by traditional calligraphers, where ink is mixed with the threads and then used. This way the ink doesn’t flow out of the container in case the jar topples. Also, it’s easier to write with the Qalam when dipped.

f3dba2c3-a9fd-5b74-903f-49b2ea0ba680.definition: Connected to blessings, meaning to whom it belongs, to the owner.

220ac6c9-5bbb-5494-a7d7-a1992e0113c3.definition: A ceramic technique in which a thin coating of metal oxide resulted in an iridescent and golden shining surface on glazed ceramics. The lustre technique was introduced to many different regions by travelling potters.

771802a5-edca-59b2-932c-9952378c6dae.definition: A natural region of the northern Sahara Desert in Ghardaïa Province, Algeria.

ff94889d-f66f-5e04-bc88-5fba2822cea4.definition: Location in southern Jordan, located 218 km from the capital Amman.

5673b322-36c7-5999-b728-0eab4e189123.definition: Large basin, could also mean patissier.

de7865d2-5988-5b78-b69f-32fb1986c355.definition: A defensive architectural feature found on the exterior of towers and gates used to pour hot oil onto enemies below. Ar. saqqata from the root *s q t*, “to drop”.

f2c933f6-93e1-5c11-a123-36ceacc8076f.definition: Comes from ضيف (*dayf*guest). A *madafa* is a building or specific room within a home designated for receiving guests.

455c1318-16a9-50f2-9c44-6643a9de238c.definition:
Theological institution that provided instruction on Islamic law (*shari’a*), jurisprudence (*fiqh*), Quran, Hadith, and Arabic, as well as accomodations for students.  
  
Today, a school. Fr. *medersa*, Tr. *medrese*.

40398059-a02d-5383-970f-ba570e4894c7.definition:
A 'mafrash' is one of the emblamatic woven handicrafts of the nomadic peoples of Iran. The weaving and use of mafrash is particularly prevalent among the nomads of the Ardabil region, as well as the Qashqai tribes. This handwoven item takes the form of a rectangular cube with a lid, resembling a box or suitcase. Nomads use it to transport quilts, mattresses, or essential items during their travels or migrations. Its transportation on the backs of pack animals is also very convenient.  
After weaving the mafrash, leather strips are sewn along the edges, and leather handles are attached to it. Nowadays, its weaving incorporates the techniques of kilim or Soumak, and its decorative patterns are often both prominent and supplementary.

0ef7f8f7-4076-532a-bb30-309094400dcb.definition: A spoon, could also mean scoop, depending on the context.

be71e06b-ee9d-56dd-9643-241707440030.definition: Maghribi calligraphy takes its name from the Arabic word "Maghribi," meaning "western," and is associated with the western Islamic regions of North Africa and Spain, where this script and its variations originated in the 10th century. Its distinguishing characteristics include descending strokes with large, sweeping curves or loops, uniform stroke thickness, the frequent use of brown ink, a horizontal baseline, flat vowel markings, and its lineage traces back to the earliest rounded script of the Arabian Peninsula.

a9dba7ef-b3dc-5e16-b084-69f0f9f4e817.definition: A cursive calligraphic style that was widespread in Muslim Spain and North Africa. It developed through the infusion of local artistic taste with *kufic* script. The best examples were produced during the AH 6th–7th / AD 12th–13th centuries under Umayyads of al-Andalus. See also calligraphy.

b1520fd2-381d-5d56-a9d2-7d019d4f34c2.definition: A richly decorated tent-like structure used on the back of a camel to transport noble ladies. Also used as a means to transport the *kiswa* in the yearly Hajj caravan sent by sovereigns to Mecca with pilgrimage delegations.

060fddee-5dfb-5fcb-a8e2-9adf565f8bfd.definition: A keeper and driver of an elephant.

2c82480a-44bd-565c-9d5c-7b38307ae24e.definition: Tin-glazed earthenware with painting on unfired glaze, typical of Spain and Italy, and believed to have been influenced by Islamic pottery techniques.

4d0ea53b-609e-5e3d-817e-8067fab67fc3.definition: (pl. majalis). Meeting hosted by the ruler or a high official. Designate also the audience hall in which the assembly was held.

b8d16d41-1432-570b-9412-811f1725b1bb.definition: Makhzan al-Asrar is the renowned title of a Mathnawi written by the Persian poet Nizami Ganjavi. This collection represents the initial part of Nizami Ganjavi's most famous work, "Khamsa of Nizami," and stands as a notable instance of didactic literature.

a37a6b9d-ede1-5960-8830-f900244aa585.definition: Pen-cutting slab, (also spelled as *maqta*) a small sab sometimes made of bone used to cut the tip of the bamboo or reed Qalam.

9e4b2650-05be-581f-8706-c2064eac74ce.definition:
A traditional elementary school that historically taught Quran, reading, writing, and basic Islamic studies. See also *kuttab*.  
  
Tr. *mektep*, *sıbyan mektebi*.

c63eadcb-48c2-5d81-af64-7d25734b9638.definition:
This term has different meanings:  
  
Mala  
A Turkish word describing a particular part of town, usually used as a suffix after the name of the locality, usually a close by river, or the majority of the living population of the locality  
  
Mala  
Necklace

bd6ee598-f323-5770-a786-0151295aea83.definition: One of the four Sunni legal schools of Orthodox Islam. Founded by Imam Malik and spread throughout the western Muslim world including al-Andalus.

1e97c7b6-80de-5294-bd26-e7192b4e6889.definition:
"Braid-Work  
A thin embroidered piece ties the edges of the dress together."

991d6b1e-4feb-5ca1-b2e2-466e617e394e.definition: A ceremonial handkerchief, could also refer to a napkin.

0fa6da1f-1658-5a20-b43f-b3fdad30d66d.definition: Style of Portuguese architecture developed during the reign of Manuel I (1495–1521) and characterised by ornate elaborations of Gothic and renaissance styles.

52b16b80-e428-5bfa-a548-51e9d574cee0.definition: Open rooms without doors, situated on the sides of a patio. Egypt: Reception hall.

af45d65f-d61d-59ed-bd55-76ee503119e9.definition: Building of one or more architectural units, usually with a dome, that contains the tomb of an important religious figure. A place of worship, and pilgrimage. See also darih, *mashhad*, *qubba*, *türbe*.

a6126354-463d-5810-881f-8b80507aa06b.definition: Known as Maqsud Kashani, he likely held the position of a court official responsible for creating carpets during the Safavid era.

5f70c6f4-762e-5438-bf74-53c9daaa431c.definition: Area of sanctuary in congregational mosques reserved for the caliph or the *imam* during public prayer times. Also, a place in a public building that is set aside for private use (as found in a *hammam*). Fr. *maqsoura*.

f2ec79dc-0998-56d5-8cc2-bce2d4228e77.definition:
Building of one or more architectural units, usually with a dome, that contains the tomb of an important religious figure. A place of worship, and pilgrimage. See also darih, mashhad, qubba, türbe.  
Additionally, Mashhad, alternatively spelled as Mashad or Meshed, serves as the city and capital of the Khorasan-e Razavi province in north-eastern Iran.  
  
See also darih, *maqam*, *qubba*, *türbe*.

3bcfdeb5-5c8a-58e9-8dfd-9ad2a9f98fdb.definition: Wooden lattice screens made of turned pieces of wood assembled to form a window grille. Fr: *machrabiyya*. Tr. *meşrebiye*.

f176a992-6546-55ba-a3e5-6877adc61b76.definition: Literally, “place of prostration”. A mosque where daily prayers are held, usually with the exception of the Friday prayers, which cannot take place in a *meşrebiye* owing to the absence of a *minbar*. Tr. *mescit*. See also *jami’*.

a04d4101-e499-5fb8-ad85-ae402c6b673f.definition: A long stone protruding ledge or bench against an outer wall on either side of entrance to a building.

f8e3e6f3-0c4c-5fbc-987d-0aef995ecc42.definition: Ottoman leather bottle, a water flask, usually considered as a pilgrim’s flask.

0cdf2b3a-f444-5757-a5d7-009cdb4ac1b7.definition: (Turkish *Mevlid) Birthday of the Prophet. Along with being referred to as the celebration of the birth of Muhammad, the term Mawlid refers to the "text especially composed for and recited at Muhammad's nativity celebration" or "a text recited or sung on that day".*

e99f9b90-c624-5aa1-815f-a47f478f7da3.definition: Town, the old quarter, self-sufficient city centre. Also the name of a city in Saudi Arabia where the Muslims migrated in AD 622 and where the Prophet Muhammad is buried.

28865fe0-58a5-5999-9b3f-6e5cf3787e6a.definition: Simple decoration of wooden triangles in the corners, creating hexagons.

32178605-4854-58d8-b7b4-f35cf3cf68f4.definition: Ascension of the Great Prophet Muhammad to Heaven to the throne of Allah, where he received the divine instruction for the five daily prayers (*salat*) for Muslims. Along with Muhammad’s night journey *Isrāʾ from the “sacred place of worship” (Mecca) to the “further place of worship” (Jerusalem), the Mi’raj creates the two parts of the night journey of Muhammad.*

8d2b9746-8e9b-5ac7-8c70-6fd0cd7e3667.definition: The hall next to a mosque where ritual ablutions take place.

e7f7d170-9ce3-5eb5-8c00-b201155164d8.definition: Arched niche, usually concave but sometimes flat, in religious Islamic buildings indicating the direction of Mecca, which worshippers face when praying.

1eec6d02-be45-5c34-aad1-32d6dd772a28.definition:
A designation for fritware pottery made at Kashan/Iran which uses enamel colours on a differently coloured ground (white, turquoise etc.) for ornamental and figural painting and inscriptions.  
  
Minakari, also known as Minai, is a traditional Persian enamelworking technique, distinguished by intricate designs and vibrant colours. This art form involves applying colourful enamel paints onto metal surfaces, such as copper, and then firing them in a kiln to achieve a glossy and durable finish. Minakari often features intricate patterns, floral motifs, and other details, creating visually captivating pieces of art. It has been used to embellish various objects, including pottery, vases, plates, and jewellery, and holds cultural significance as a celebrated art form in Iran.
