a7da3b34-cced-5cac-bca5-7cde2160fdbf.definition: A stepped pulpit for delivering the sermon during the Friday prayers and the first morning prayers during the two big Muslim feasts. It is placed to the right of the *mihrab* in a mosque. *minbar*s first appeared in the Umayyad period.

016aabef-bd66-5afb-8b53-eec9959e0d50.definition: The Ming dynasty ruled in China 1368–1644. Blue-and-white Ming porcelain is distinguished by the integration of dragon motifs with floral compositions. See also Chinoiserie.

3e264948-1277-58b6-8c2d-a082884fee44.definition: Mirza Baba, hailing from the Imami family in Isfahan, was an Iranian artist employed at the Tehran court during the rule of Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar and Fath-Ali Shah Qajar.

0c051692-aaa6-5bc3-9767-1917d3208074.definition: Weight standard for gold dinars (4,25 g), established during the reign of Abd’ al-Malik of the Umayyad dynasty.

b2f40fe6-7d9e-55fe-91fd-b02fa7f5b5a2.definition: In the Christian kingdoms of the Peninsula the name given to Muslims who formally converted to Christianity after the Reconquista.

d9555abf-9d44-5fae-95f4-b894702cfcd9.definition: From Ar. *must‘arab*. A member of the Christian minorities, tolerated by Muslim rulers as tributaries, who lived in al-Andalus holding on to their religion and ecclesiastic and judicial organisation.

a26fcbf5-43f5-53e6-8d77-b2efc78c5302.definition: Funerary stele which is usually made out of marble. Mqabriya is an equivalent of a tomb stone.

bac9d185-bb86-5b2d-b50d-fd876fb0fe78.definition: Location in Algeria. It is the capital of the province of the same name.

432a631d-9c77-5598-9224-35e8479385c8.definition: (Pl. *murabitun*) A religious Muslim, sanctified by asceticism, whose tomb is a place of pilgrimage; a warrior-monk living in a *ribat*. The name of a dynasty known in English as Almoravid that ruled al-Andalus AH 454–541 / AD 1062–1147. Fr. *mourabit*, *mourabitoun*.

b01a26b1-9ff1-5e29-aedd-bb4316a59907.definition: A volume measuring instrument that has been widely used as a reference measure in the Islamic region for the payment of *zakat*, *fidya* and *kaffara*. Many well-known literatures have their own definition of the mudd, but never being discussed technically in term of volume calibration. It equals to 628 ml (KSA).

9c8d51a2-cb58-59b3-92e4-fecb1ca87eb4.definition: From Ar. *mudajjan*. Muslims who were allowed to remain among their Christian conquerors, without changing their religion, in exchange for tribute. The adjective Mudéjar is also used to describe traditional craftsmanship begun under Islamic domination and continued for Christian clients after the Christian conquest.

b9deabe4-38f9-5144-9eed-f59423fe7ddc.definition: Muslim religious official charged with announcing from the mosque minaret the five prayers of the day. *Müezzin mahfili*: Tr., special platform for the *muezzin*s. See also *adhan*.

95cd8cc7-61c1-518d-a3d1-397850242e35.definition: A Muslim legal expert who is empowered to give rulings on religious matters.

323fc8b6-ea1a-5717-982f-38123c87161c.definition:
Muhaqqaq is an Islamic calligraphic style that emerged in the 10th century and was employed widely in the Islamic world for creating elaborate, large Qur'ans and architectural inscriptions. Its defining characteristics include a precise, angular script with upright letters, meticulously balanced ascenders and horizontal elements, a distinct horizontal emphasis (wider than it is tall), descending strokes terminating in straight, sharp points rather than curving upwards, and the frequent use of descending round strokes that encircle the following letter. Muhaqqaq is typically employed in combination with "Rayhani," a smaller rendition of the same script.  
  
A large cursive script related to the *naskhi* script used in the Middle Ages. It is one of the six basic styles of writing. Tr. *muhaqqaq*. See also calligraphy.

82fdfe6b-967a-5cb6-9f9f-9454dbda5454.definition: A burnishing tool used by calligraphers and miniaturist painters to burnish the paper as well as pure gold leaf.

89bfc871-8edd-5e4f-81e0-fe5ff704e5e9.definition: Muin Musavvir was a prominent Persian miniaturist during the 17th century in Safavid Iran. It is believed that he was born around AH 1018- 1024 / AD 1610-1615. Mu‘in Musavvir received his artistic education under Reza Abbasi, who was the preeminent painter of that era. It is thought that he probably passed away in AH 1104 / AD 1693.

23ba4d6b-6ce4-504a-b495-efdcb419b6ed.definition: Literally the "chosen one". This term designate the person responsible for the clan or tribe; typically an elder.

cfc9414f-7ca4-5e8a-80ea-d0fc4865d5c9.definition: From Ar. *muwallad*. Christians who were converted to Islamism and lived as Muslims during the domination of the Arabs in the Iberian Peninsula.

4c8c2130-e69d-5ae6-b03b-7dc72bf78f7a.definition: Kingdom or sovereignty. The word is often applied in calligraphic ornamentation to decorate courtly items.

bd2ffd1a-1d12-5fc1-ab6b-b186e0622cb6.definition: Stalactite- or honeycomb-like architectural ornamentation which adorns many surfaces including domes and corbels. In the Maghreb *muqarbas*. Fr. *mouqarnas*.

032d07d0-de44-5fc4-b2ac-8712cfaa0838.definition: Muraqqa is the Persian term for an album of paintings and calligraphy.

b43d4539-8c8e-5de3-ba56-a72f1632c7c8.definition: Meaning "bitter", often used to describe coffee.

9f4d1152-e032-5509-a8f6-ac7d6117d2d3.definition: An Arabic word for a codex or collection of sheets, but also refers to a written copy of the Quran.

3a840421-ce84-5045-8ad3-f9355dd51baf.definition: Woodwind instrument, similar to a pan flute.

265d620f-7648-5a86-8f6f-c5f7a71b3934.definition: The palace workshop established by Fatih Sultan Mehmed in the 15th century in Topkapi Palace, located outside the Bab-i Hümayûn, next to Arslanhane.

5fe19010-9046-582a-a119-66c4870348e7.definition: Tr. Muslim ritual prayers exercised five times a day. *Namazgah*: an open-air place on inter-city roads or recreation areas for performing the *namaz*.

8ffa05a8-a165-5e2c-b72e-27e8d5f953ac.definition: Literally “copied”. One of the most widespread styles of Islamic calligraphy used in Qur’ans and other books. It combines the flexibility of the *farsi* style with the harmony of the *kufic* script. Tr. *nesih*.

ea137b2c-4b18-5db2-bba2-703e333c897d.definition: Whilst prevailing belief is that Naskh calligraphy emerged in 310 AH (922-23 AD), recent research suggests it evolved from the Kufic script that dates back to the early days of Islam. Over time, Naskh supplanted Kufic as the preferred script for the Qur'an. Today, Naskh is the dominant script used in Qur'an transcription, surpassing all other scripts combined due to its enhanced legibility.

ddabdcad-fe35-518d-a9c0-32923e6bd220.definition:
One the most widespread styles of Arabic calligraphy (with *thuluth* and *naskhi*), developed by Persian calligraphers. A stronger and more stylish form of *ta’liq*, it is characterised by its rounded forms, clarity and geometrical purity. Although written without vowel marks it was much favoured as it was easy to read. Tr. *nestalik*.  
  
Emerged as the prominent form of Persian calligraphy during the 15th and 16th centuries. This cursive style was a fusion of the naskhi and taʿliq scripts, characterised by elongated horizontal strokes and exaggerated rounded shapes. In nastaʿliq, diacritical marks were informally positioned, and lines flowed with a curvaceous grace rather than adhering to a strict straightness. This script often found its way into the artwork of the early Safavid era (16th century) and is traditionally regarded as the most refined among Persian calligraphic styles.

d99278fb-cfa3-513e-9af1-4e39e27f241b.definition: A technique used in metalwork, where engraved areas are filled with a mixture of different materials such as lead, copper and silver. Fr. *niel*.

901f2d10-a163-54d9-9db6-576def5054df.definition: An adjective indicating the person's place of origin, tribal affiliation, or ancestry, used at the end of the name.

459f8079-3081-520c-95f1-def76fceb958.definition: Stringed musical instrument prominent in medieval and modern Islamic music. It is the parent of the European lute. The oud has a deep pear-shaped body, a fretless fingerboard.

7798ae44-cdad-53a4-a9a8-b430d59ba21f.definition: A device made from a forked branch to which one wrist is attached by an additional band of wood or metal.

d030499b-007d-57d0-8e57-9c741e288906.definition: Central roundel used in Suzani carpentry

09da9b9a-2f44-5b44-8b45-91810cc84650.definition: Term used to describe leopard or tiger stripes when used as a pattern for textile.

ea9e06ca-7872-5541-9ac2-11302f8890c2.definition: A Turkish honorific title, arabicised as *Basha*.

60068ca4-be84-58d0-a590-341306ae5e41.definition: Pearls, the only organic material considered to be precious gemstones, can be widely divided into two categories: natural and cultivated. The formation of the pearl occurs when a foreign body such as a grain of sand or a parasite enters the shell of an oyster or mussel. Due to their very specific origin, pearls have come to be focal points of many legends and myths. Because of their circular shape, they are frequently associated with the moon. They can also symbolize life in general, as well as birth. Some old beliefs state that morning dew, when hardened, turns into pearls. Civilizations from areas with pearl fishing cultures, such as the Middle East and Asia, have for centuries viewed pearls as symbols of supremacy, innocence and female charm.

da0667e3-f262-5c61-b878-0b63eed0381b.definition: Motifs in the shapes of leopard spots or tiger stripes.

ba7ec4e5-ec62-5bf2-bd27-6b932bb32ca1.definition: A small box or lidded container used for holding a variety of objects such as medicine, writing instruments, etc.

a2005bd2-bdc7-54c7-b3c5-a7cd040e82bc.definition: Reception hall where guests are received.

dc0561a2-2592-560f-8a87-20cd58a96753.definition:
"Chest Panel  
From the head of the right shoulder to the end of the left shoulder."

644520d0-0549-5413-aad0-2115f7fb372a.definition: Writing instrument in the form of a brush, usually made out of bamboo or reed, predominantly used for calligraphy.

ee81ae22-7465-5b41-93e7-a5b7a2efeb7c.definition: A fabric painting technique. The word is derived from the Persian words *ghalam* (pen) and *kari* (craftmanship), meaning drawing with a pen (*Ghalamkar*).

21baedfe-a3af-5ec7-b036-b47426bdc117.definition: A title given to a saint who is at a very high level of spirituality. They are different from other saints and have very strong feelings of love for God's creation. Qalandars, among the saints, are those persons who may enjoy freedom from the ties and bounds of time and space.

3569da80-2a51-50bb-afca-141112480550.definition: A term used only in Tunisia for Ottoman-inspired polychrome pottery for architectural decoration produced in an area in the city of Tunis called Qallalin.

7978d46e-780e-5ff3-b397-3e8bfd533787.definition: (Pl. *qanawat*) Subterranean conduit of water; part of a distributory network.

59b4beee-e4d9-52ef-99f1-2a66945a3694.definition: A term for glazed tile panels derived from the Iranian city of Kashan, where tiles to decorate buildings had been produced since the Seljuq period. The term was used by the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battutah in Iran for the tile panels that reminded him of the *zellij* tiles of the Maghreb.

44366451-8359-541a-9be5-8dc8351d0c81.definition: The qasida is the most prestigious poetical creation throughout Arab history. Even nowadays it is deemed the ultimate work of artistic achievement of Arab culture. It is a tripartite composition that follows a thematic sequence. The traditional qasida, its form, and its content, have remained influential not only for Arabic literature, but also for later developments in Turkish and Persian literature.

c47920b0-c22e-53d0-aa8c-93eb3956ca0e.definition: From Latin *castrum*. Palace, castle. *Qusayr*: diminutive form of *qasr*. Tr. kasr. See also *bayt*, dar.

f37cbff8-b219-59af-940c-6d009539e2a7.definition: Covered market for precious merchandise (gold, silk, etc.). See also *arasta*, *bazaar*, *bedesten*, *suq*.

0089ce74-d5cd-57d2-bbe4-c8de79b156c9.definition: Direction of the Ka‘ba in Mecca, which Muslims face during prayer. The qibla wall of the mosque is where the *mihrab* is situated.

ea03a56c-d809-5ee0-9bf3-d2601be89fe3.definition: A portable astronomical instrument whose name literally means "showing the direction to the Ka'ba". The alternative name for it is astrolabe.

6eb8238b-896d-5482-a234-198b4db17f4d.definition: Arabic term used to describe oil lamps, could also refer to any form of lamp, such as a candlestick or a lantern.

c39cd815-3b51-5b89-a4e4-5e9f2c0ca622.definition: Dome; by extension a monument or chamber built over the grave of a saint or important person, which is usually marked with a dome. Fr. *koubba*. Tr. *kubbe* (dome only).

9c6aeb81-7bc2-5ea4-9209-1c4a1345ac29.definition: The division of the Qur’an into 30 parts. Each part (*juz’*) was bound as a separate volume and usually the 30 volumes were housed in an illuminated box.

1f1c56a0-2af0-51fc-9adb-3b2cb1118d0b.definition: From Ar. *rabad*. Quarter outside the walls.

389ffbb1-3a7e-5ec3-a9fc-efdd3e0f54ca.definition: The fourth month of the Islamic calendar. Its name means  the 'second spring'.

79ad5742-3251-5a48-afdc-3eadbe4bc902.definition: The ninth month of the Hijri / lunar calendar when Muslims fast. It is the last of the three consecutive holy months. Tr. Ramazan.

87260489-dd79-59f8-a295-dd2d8f65524a.definition: A term used widely and sometimes very generally for pottery from the Syrian town of Raqqa. Raqqa ware includes different pottery such as dark brown lustreware and, fritware with monochrome or polychrome underglaze painting.

2f088e48-669e-5b0f-b7ef-a94fb24641eb.definition:
Rayhani is a calligraphic style that was used for copying Qur’ans. It is characterised by its smaller rendition of muhaqqaq, featuring letter forms with sharper, more pointed shapes compared to naskh, and often distinguished by a prominent spike on the initial alif-lam letter shape.  
  
Although this script shows close resemblance to *muhaqqaq*, it is written on a smaller scale. It was used in large Qur’ans produced in AH 7th–8th / AD 13th–14th centuries. See also calligraphy.

30f08fe7-8bb1-504a-aa55-685d583ff5ba.definition: Reconquest of the Iberian Peninsula (Spain and Portugal) by the Christians from the Muslims, which ended in AH 897 / AD 1492 with the fall of Granada.

44b5dcf7-b45d-5206-b3e1-f77d5f220d80.definition: A metalworking technique. To make a design appear in relief on the front of a metal work of art, it has to be worked in repoussé (hammered) from the back.

732e2f9b-afda-508f-9938-c167d92f40f2.definition: Reza Abbasi was a renowned Persian artist associated with the Esfahan school. He held a special place as the preferred painter of Shah Abbas I, often referred to as Shah Abbas the Great. Reza Abbasi was born around AH 977 / AD 1570 in Mashhad, which was part of Safavid Iran. His father, Ali Asghar of Kashan, was an artist who worked in the court of Prince Ibrahim Mirza, the Safavid viceroy in Mashhad. During that period (AH 963- 984 / AD 1556-1577), Mashhad was a prominent hub for the development of the arts in Iran.

9a8096ea-a204-590a-8744-2ddf28c2b6b8.definition: Fortified enclosure for religious warriors (North Africa); a hospice for pilgrims (Mamluk Egypt, Palestine and Syria). The name of the town Rabat comes from Ribat al-Fath (Ribat of the Conquest).

41cfc342-d602-582b-a279-22302f06909d.definition: The term "Riqa" originates from the Arabic word "ruq’a," which translates to "a fragment or a small piece of fabric." This name was assigned to the script because it was frequently used for writing on small paper fragments, often in petitions addressed to royalty.

8f56e049-19ca-5856-9caa-3acff60817b3.definition: Pl. of *rawda* “garden”. Always used in plural form, in Morocco *riyad* means a garden within residential housing.

9b3eb14d-ccb9-5bdf-b3a6-ae4fd27367cf.definition: Rosewater is a fragrant liquid crafted by immersing rose petals in water. Prior to the advancement of the distillation method for producing rosewater, Persian cuisine already employed rose petals to enhance the aroma and taste of dishes. Rose water likely had its beginnings in Persia, where it was identified as "gulab". The technique of steam distillation to create rosewater was perfected by Persian chemist, Ibn Sina/ Avicenna, within the medieval Islamic world.

e86b778e-eb99-506f-b636-43526557b90f.definition:
"Rubies are red colored gemstones made of aluminium oxide, and they come from the mineral group of corundum. Like other gemstones, they are formed deep under the Earth’s surface, but at a shallower depth than most. Rubies owe their notable red color to the presence of chromium oxide during crystal formation. Rubies rank relatively low on the Mohs scale (used to measure mineral hardness), and therefore require extra attention when being polished and set into jewelry.  
Due to its vivid color, the stone is the ultimate symbol of fire, and it symbolizes humility, kindness and godly love. It is considered the most precious gemstone in India and the Hindu religion, where it is referred to as the *Ratna Raj*, or “Queen of All Gemstones”. Islamic tradition has similar symbolism in the story of Abraham’s ruby, which was brought to Kabba by Archangel Michael but has been transformed into a black stone due to the sins of the human race. It is believed that this ruby has eyes, ears and a tongue, and therefore can witness for the righteous in the Last Judgement. As a gemstone that equally represents religious and secular power, it was frequently present on crowns of Christian monarchs, as a symbol of Christ’s blood."

99e11148-863b-5916-afb5-d3b71fb5abe5.definition: Split-palmette motif. One of the most popular and basic motifs in Islamic decorative arts, applied to every medium from woodcarving to tiles. It is mostly seen in arabesques. It was named after an earlier name for Anatolia.

310bd3c5-0e81-53d5-8263-8bca44c8007a.definition: A calligraphic style suitable for writing fast used by the Ottoman administration in *waqf* documents, letters, the last prayer pages of the Qur’ans and the diplomas of calligraphy students (hence also called ijaza (diploma) script). Today it is generally used in Arab daily newspapers for the headlines. See also calligraphy.

1708f744-b3be-5ca3-8384-d8109f48190c.definition: Ruzbihan Mohammad al-Shirazi, a renowned calligrapher and illuminator from Shiraz, was active in the first half of the 10th AH century. His full name is Ruzbihan Muhammad al-Tab‘i al-Shirazi. Although the exact dates of his birth and death are not known, based on his dated and historical works, his period of activity is presumed to be between AH 915-968 / AD 1509-1561. One of the distinctive features of Ruzbihan Mohammad's illumination is his meticulous craftsmanship and use of gentle colours. According to records, in a preserved Quran located in the National Museum of Iran, his father, Hajji Na'im al-Din, was a scribe and illuminator who produced multiple copies in the second half of the 9th century.

0d914aeb-4f85-55c7-874c-71b1090e5fec.definition: Crafted within the confines of Shiraz, this magnificent Qur'an stands as an exceptional representation of the book arts during the 16th century in Iran. The revered master-calligrapher, Ruzbihan, undertook the task of inscribing the sacred text, employing three distinct scripts for the core content and employing additional calligraphic forms for the titles of chapters.

85c2ecc8-51b1-5e22-90ca-051cf297fa08.definition:
"Sleeve  
From the beginning of the palm to the middle of the elbow."

a8525513-1742-5e9f-85de-bb2067ad9fb6.definition:
(Pl. *subul* or *asbila*) Small structures that were designed to dispense and provide free and clean drinking water to the public. *Sabil*s can be freestanding buildings or parts of small or large charitable complexes.  
  
Tr. sebil – a chamber where an attendant serves free drink to the public.

8f59f848-6089-5df5-ac39-251f4a455901.definition: Often a two-story structure where the ground level is reserved for the *sabil* (public water source) and the upper level is the elementary school or *kuttab*.

e379842a-f861-5764-9e7e-5721988f80fb.definition: Heavy military sword with a long cutting edge and, often, a curved blade.

469f9c24-c7f1-53c1-89e9-cee0ebd1e160.definition: Manuscripts of a particular format are known by the term safina, a Persian word meaning "boat" and an apparent reference to their long and narrow, boat-like shape. Safinas were presumably designed to be carried in the pocket, and most are anthologies of verse.

e83fa4a5-45f3-5663-8489-ce86086e6417.definition: Term used for a prayer rug. It could mean prostration or prostrate, and also may refer to a mark in the text of the Quran.

ab5197e2-ba37-5f84-9a8c-1bc168852cbc.definition: Meaning blessings, pl. of the word Salam. Could also refer to safety.

63187e27-a423-515a-905c-73fa1d04ccf8.definition: This general term is used for the different styles in stucco common in the temporary Abbasid capital of Samarra in Iraq. Style A uses naturalistic designs, Style B uses naturalistic designs interwoven with abstract designs and Style C uses barely discernible plant design with bevelled edges in an abstract way.

cd199074-1609-59ce-b475-3e9de72ddb82.definition: Samite was a luxurious and heavy silk fabric worn throughout the Middle Ages made of a twill-type (diagonal weave pattern) and  was often embellished with gold or silver thread.

f1179b47-7c52-5959-8dd5-1c6e4daa568d.definition:
This term has different meanings:  
  
Sanjak  
Designated province in the Ottoman Empire  
  
Sanjak  
Shield-shaped banner

408f6907-26a4-5d58-888d-84a60755db29.definition: Sapphires come from the corundum group of minerals, and rank highly on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness. Today the term Sapphire refers to all corundum stones that are not red. The most common sapphires are blue, yet they can also be green, yellow or colorless. Sapphires, much like their cousins rubies, have a series of legends and myths about them. They are primarily associated with immortality and innocence, and are called the gemstone of the heavens. The Persians believed that the world stood on a giant sapphire, whose magnificent color radiated through the universe. The Egyptians and Romans considered the sapphire to be the gemstone of truth and justice, while in the Catholic church it is considered the ultimate symbol of godly light.

33cef020-667f-52b7-8e7c-a6746c1827af.definition: High court official responsible for overseeing food and drink service or servant providing drinks or entertainment. The sultan had several cupbearers led by the *Saqi al-sultan* (chief cupbearer). The *saqi was represented by the symbol of a cup.*

7b0b0e45-2f2a-5fd0-be86-16fa0e895a59.definition: In the Maghreb an entrance to a house, often twisting and turning.

2b842401-a74c-58e4-bd5e-da8fc318e324.definition: A large tube or length of fabric, often wrapped around the waist.

2b6ccae8-75c6-5d20-8c47-82474d8ded78.definition: A turban ornament that was worn by significant Hindu, Sikh and Muslim princes.

0f26046e-3b67-5601-baf6-72d291d77ad0.definition: Straight, double-edged sword. The sayf varied in appearance throughout Islamic history.

98f32a82-0f8d-523b-b82b-b4c5d2090590.definition: (Pl. *sada*) Descendants of Prophet Muhammad. See also *sharif*.

9ba68a24-0e40-52cc-9957-968da7055d9a.definition: Arabic title of respect, meaning Heir to the grandson of the prophet Muhammad.

e6ca4b0f-8824-5172-9b8e-6f572fcd1de7.definition: A term applied to different works of Ottoman art from AH 960–1010 / AD 1555–1600 that show a repertoire of leaves, flowers and palmettes with imaginary creatures such as dragons. The style uses curving lines and owes much to calligraphy. It is found in album drawings, ceramics, metalwork, textiles and carpets.

405f1bc4-d301-552c-8f10-fc6e68168f45.definition: A Prayer rug. It varies in size and decoration.

11864cd8-7574-5b81-8dbd-f0180dc203cf.definition: The writer of *Şehname*, equivalent to a court historian.

d9561d95-09e3-53a8-a3d9-022df6d80d3b.definition: Type of Ottoman silk fabrics, usually woven in designs and motifs quite different from the typical Ottoman artistic language, organized in narrow horizontal bands of small-scale decoration.

1e2bc98b-db88-5155-9556-2e6e52c00a36.definition: Mobile openwork plaque or rete, could also mean net.

1c72befa-b751-593e-8d75-c600c4e562d3.definition: A wall fountain attached to a wall. Tr. *Şadırvan*, a şadırvan is a fountain, especially for ablutions in a mosque courtyard. It can be part of a wall or free-standing.

03eaf2d5-1988-549b-919f-2aaad8416221.definition: One of the four Sunni legal schools of Orthodox Islam. Tr. *Şafi*.

970967ba-4fb4-5316-b273-742dafe6d401.definition: One of the four Sunni schools of religious law.

5dfb0beb-240c-5fb8-a4ba-14bd15936137.definition: Title of the kings of Iran, or Persia. The title shah was also used in Afghanistan until the overturn of the monarchy in 1973 and has been used by rulers and princelings in other countries of central and southern Asia.

b574ce4b-f297-5c3f-b370-895a19b2933a.definition: Written by the Persian poet Ferdowsi, the Shahnama or Shahnameh is a long epic poem which dwells on the mythical and historical past of the Persian Empire.

6d92f187-6403-5612-9082-88dde5497f13.definition: An intricately decorated rosette or medallion which is used in many contexts, including manuscripts, carpets, ornamental metalwork and architectural decoration such as the underside of domes. It can take several overall shapes, from circles to stars. It can also mean the Sun.

72c54743-5b69-565e-b54d-8fe9dfa0e746.definition: Window, also could refer to an umbrella.

bd727956-74e1-5614-9f39-07003f768b6a.definition: Literally, “road”. Islamic precepts that the believer must follow in order to be on the right road that leads to God. The *Shari‘a* rules the behaviour of the faithful in the spiritual, legal, social and political spheres, and also in the concrete aspects of daily life.

119946d4-3087-5314-b4ea-dcffb40a90c2.definition: Double-reed wind instrument of Middle Eastern origin, a precursor of the oboe.

724abd8d-f15f-5718-b5ea-313655eea65a.definition: One of the most complex types of pileless weaving. In addition to warp and weft threads, various coloured threads are interwoven into the “body” creating an intricate and highly spectacular pattern.

a0a0b21a-5425-5de1-8d04-b7fd7daeca8b.definition: An elder, respected for his knowledge and age, learned man instructed in the religious sciences, member of a religious brotherhood, sufi master. Tr. *Şeyh*. Shaykh al-Islam: The head of the hierarchy of the doctors of Muslim canon law, tradition and theology. Tr. Şeyhülislam.

c98013e1-9336-5b90-9d71-2658cca1e0ca.definition: (Pl. *shurafa*) Descendant of the Prophet Muhammad. See also *sayyed*.

3f35b372-188c-5440-a3a1-24902734c0d8.definition: Member of the smaller of the two major branches of Islam, the Shiʿa, distinguished from the majority Sunnis.

3d198a73-3a55-5a34-b209-561c8dc2c58e.definition: Correctly, Shi‘at ‘Ali, meaning “the party of ‘Ali”. Shi‘ites rejected the legitimacy of all caliphs who succeed after the assassination of Ali (AH 40 / AD 661), the Prophet’s cousin and son-in-law. See also Sunna.

3f7cde9b-cf8d-5b7b-a648-991f1fc4345f.definition: A hunter, or a guide for hunting expeditions.

1a911f25-2169-5473-b48f-e5e9bf7e6aff.definition: A culturally significant city in southern Iran, often referred to as the "City of Poets" and "City of Gardens." This is because of its numerous lush gardens, including the famous Eram Garden, and for being the hometown of renowned Persian poets, such as Hafez and Saadi. Shiraz is also known for its historical sites, including the Nasir al-Mulk Mosque and the Tomb of Cyrus the Great.

619209ad-bef6-58a2-a777-4ddd92b2d94f.definition: Refers to the “lotus tree” in the Quran. The Sidrat al-Muntaha marks the celestial boundary between those who attain the highest place in heaven (prophets, angels) and Allah (the divine).

947c308d-bc24-5bbc-91e5-bb461cbe7cfa.definition: Bearer of arms, an official of the court who was in charge of the preservation and maintenance of arms.

6d2d57b7-54c2-5423-bd0e-5cb6f4137078.definition: Genealogy, with Silsila signifying a genealogy in the form of a chain, as opposed to the one formed as a tree ( *sharaja*).

717dbbdd-a73f-5072-9370-1b0902785426.definition: A huge ancient bird of Persian legend credited with possessing great wisdom.

ea7ba680-cfdb-5f45-9030-dd43782bebb2.definition: A style of Islamic calligraphy originating from China for using the Arabic script. It gained importance and fame through its hybrid style, and its historic value is related to the hybrid nature of the Chinese Muslim ethnic group, known as the Hui. It can also refer to Chinese ceramics.

88ea725b-ca76-5d06-9ede-29e288e0ff44.definition: Knotwork based on a twelve-star pattern, and could also be used in architecture as a decorative pattern.

288b2150-8838-5cdf-8779-d98b7d476915.definition: The Sira are the prophetic biographies.  In addition to what is written in the Quran and Hadith, the sira also provide information on Muhammed's life and the early period of Islam.

4095b9ca-bfcf-5272-8d82-6416939a526f.definition: Trousers with a distinctively wide and low crotch until the knees.

60d18096-8ef8-5848-9e25-fc081e078906.definition: A wash of diluted clay applied to a ceramic vessel to cover the clay body before applying decoration.

1296cfdc-d33f-5cb5-8260-c31331325ee5.definition: The term socarrat ("scorched") refers to large fired-earth tiles manufactured using the biscuit technique: the slab, once dried in air, is rubbed with white clay on its smooth side, then blue, red ochre and iron is painted onto this base. It is then fired, and the tile comes out coloured blue, vermilion and black on a white base. They were intended to decorate eaves and cornices, to which they afforded a colourful intensity, usually in mineral earthy black tones and iron or ochre reds dissolved in a lime milk that, once set, gave them consistency.

cc6539b5-6a87-5bb1-bf6f-15172aea31c8.definition: Turkish word of Arabic origin, used for referring to any type of floor spread, but also short-legged tables commonly placed in dining rooms for eating.

eaf333b6-6e35-501e-bf90-a9642172c19b.definition: Also known as Star or Seal of Solomon / Süleyman. A motif of interlocking broken or curving lines, similar to the Star of David.

a4d72e8b-593a-5cec-9714-7483be1380d4.definition: Method of brocading handmade flat-woven rugs and similar fabrics. It is one of the oldest known techniques, identified among charred 7th-century-bc fragments excavated at Gordion, near Ankara in Anatolia.

bb7f5775-e2f9-58e9-94d3-c5e8eb594fa4.definition: A technique for decorating pottery vessels using different colours beneath or on a lead glaze. During the firing process the colours spread irregularly, as if splashed on the body.

8d51b0ae-13b3-5a75-acf3-79e63e2bd891.definition: An arch placed diagonally at each corner of a square and filled decoratively with a variety of methods, providing the transition from the cubical walls to the sphere of the dome.

b68f8c65-978e-5a31-bb68-5994ae43ec75.definition: A Muslim acetic and mystic who represents the mystical aspect of Islam.

ddce3372-545d-5166-8dfc-c8bb72ab9fe8.definition: An Islamic mystical or ascetic order. Derived from *suf*, wool, which is the fabric in which devotees (*sufi*) clothe themselves. Fr. *soufisme*.

aea62142-bf4f-5655-8c52-b1e856151ce7.definition: Honorary title used by independent sovereigns (in particular Ottomans and Seljuks) whose authority, however, does not question the nominal superiority recognised to the ruling caliph.

ab99a408-a9e3-547f-9a94-45b205e6a57b.definition: Sultan Muḥammad, who lived during the 16th century in Safavid Iran, is regarded as one of the most exceptional Persian painters and stands out as the most prominent artist of the Safavid school based in Tabriz, Iran. Between AH 900- 928 / AD 1495 and 1522, Sultan Muḥammad likely held a preeminent position within the Turkmen school of painting, which was prevalent in western Iran during the reign of the Ak Koyunlu ("White Sheep") and Kara Koyunlu ("Black Sheep") Turkmens.

f21a9ff0-ae8f-5ff9-be18-36b4a4db6794.definition: State or territories that are ruled by a sultan. Sultan is a title given to the ruler of such a place.

aa9eeba9-8ad8-555a-8988-13c068bdac81.definition: Turkish word for box or chest.

811580e5-c0b8-5c27-8c10-3a3a36bee143.definition: Literally “tradition”. For Orthodox Islam, the group of traditions of the Prophet in which legal advisers and theologians find support and foundations to establish the content of Islamic law arising from the Qur’an. Sunni: Follower of Sunna. Sunnis are divided into four schools: Hanafi, Hanbali, Maliki, Shafi’i. Sunnism: a political and religious system opposed to Shi‘ism. See also Fiqh, Shi’a.

5c212d06-15e4-5918-a02d-bb0ef2c59fe1.definition: Chapter of the Qur’an. There are 114 surahs in the Qur’an. Tr. Sure.

a0ffe329-5b1c-564e-bef0-72574ebef96a.definition: A large, hand-embroidered textile panel. The word comes from the Persian word *suzan*, which means needle. Originating from nomadic tribes in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and other Central Asian countries, suzanis have become highly collectable and valued for their beautiful decoration and fine craftsmanship.

78fd8be3-f58d-5f6b-b249-3f3c97b9ef97.definition: Tabby Weave has all the character of a hand-woven silk but with a high-performance level.

665383f5-4a15-5f32-8010-a19d807b45a5.definition: Guestroom at a mosque for itinerant dervishes and other travellers. From the AH 10th / AD 16th century *tabhanes* became part of the mosque’s prayer hall.

83f6772d-09b7-5ad2-a480-9c2c0c7c4320.definition: Small board or a tablet with which a gap is covered, such as a socarrena or the front of a wooden step.

e492236b-2179-5d42-b894-3fc913a09686.definition: From Ar. *tabiya*. A wall made from mud, which is compressed between caissons. The technique was perfected further in military constructions by introducing lime mortar into the framework. Tr. *tabya*.

1a96ac8d-419a-5515-b21c-9a95109e369b.definition: Arabic term for dish or plate, probably deriving from the Turkish word *tepsi*.

b9925565-dd1a-5d2a-b600-c734be2f3586.definition: Factions or groups. The term usually refers to the disintegration of Muslim Spain into several smaller kingdoms during the 5th/11th century.

1ad49aeb-c4a6-56fa-a5db-9635fe80d767.definition: From Tr. *tekke*, literally “place where food is served free of charge”. Centre where dervishes meet, worship and live. Architectural type introduced by the Ottomans. See also *imaret*, *khan*qah, *zawiya*.

a032a946-6a59-5dc8-99e3-7006cd02ff68.definition: Arabic word used to describe a water system.

cc2bbcf5-54f0-5959-a72b-231b955a7d9c.definition:
One of the six main styles of calligraphy developed in Persia in the AH 9th / AD 15th century. Used especially for official correspondence, it is characterised by fine lines with no vowel. Tr. *talik*. See also *nasta’liq*, calligraphy.  
  
Taliq is characterised by an unauthodox use of ligatures, which connect letters on the left that typically wouldn't be joined. It features descending strokes that form loops, rounded letter shapes with pronounced variations in letter spacing, wide spacing between lines, as well as lines that ascend from right to left.

1a356d53-950f-5eca-94fd-5f222b42af1d.definition: Long-necked fretted lute played under various names from the Balkans to north-western Asia.

7a97c84e-3014-5b8e-9c95-47155de493b7.definition: A particular type of instrument, most resembling to a lyre, finding its origins in Nubia or Sudan

78053761-99e7-5b79-85ba-68c278e8c447.definition: Reforms that were propagated under the rule of Ottoman emperors Abdulmecid I and Abdulaziz between 1839 and 1876.

d60eab2d-b4d7-5c37-a166-09672f39727f.definition: ''Path of way''. A term used in Sufi practices to refer to a specific path or a specific discipline of Sufi thought following a particular master.

da8b7101-f569-5ca6-b136-b50cc01aa5c9.definition: Cylindrical container, taller than it is wide, usually made out of glass, ceramic, or earthware, with a lid. It is used specifically for packing food, perfumery, or cosmetic products.

b2155481-cc7f-58d7-9a13-f7b8d291e362.definition: The invocation of God's blessing upon the Prophet Muhammad. Could also mean entertainment.

5826611f-c015-58cb-b5aa-7aa9b979d8aa.definition: Flat wooden ceiling completely covered with strapwork decoration, which conceals the beams; cf. *alfarje*, where the beams are exposed. From Arabic *tawshih*.

df95e636-1ccf-5f43-af09-acfeaa8bdd39.definition: Circle, collar, also could be used to refer to a necklace.

0cb5ca4c-b4bd-55d8-8d21-7fe594c06fcf.definition: Tawqi is a calligraphic script, and the term is etymologically derived from the Arabic verb "waqa’a," which means "to sign." It gained this name because it was commonly employed to inscribe the signature on decrees issued by rulers. Primarily used for scrolls, diplomas, royal documents, and impressive calligraphic works, Tawqi is frequently written alongside riqa, a smaller version of the same script. Developed in the 10th century, Tawqi is characterised by its more compressed and rounded letters, the practice of unauthorised ligatures to connect non-connecting letters on the left for faster writing, and notably shorter ascending and deeply curved horizontal strokes.

c8f3bbcb-a8cd-550d-87a2-e50f399b9921.definition: The Arabic-language name for the Torah within its context as an Islamic holy book believed by Muslims to have been given by God to the prophets and messengers amongst the Children of Israel.

578e11f8-5c8f-5ac5-80a9-a6e15ee99655.definition: Dish, could also refer to a cup or a small container of various materials, mostly round or cylindrical in shape with a handle.

950b9741-65c7-56dc-84fa-f599f1697a4f.definition: Sacred formula of entreaty to God, could also refer to a talisman.

5ee94e12-9407-5e41-bdce-43a98dc9b5bf.definition: Turkish word for centre where dervishes meet, worship and live. See also *imaret*, *khanqah*, *takiyya*, *zawiya*.

09f713d8-279f-5781-b4b0-b3e3ec8c7848.definition: Mirror trim usually used as a mirror dressing or could be used as a scarf.

a48689cf-e986-5b48-b5d7-7a78a0d35934.definition: A type of Persian (Iranian) handwoven cloth, produced primarily in the Isfahan province.

0286f96a-fc62-506d-a042-ab44ef3b40b1.definition: A type of geometric decoration used for tiles.

0b7b13a1-8533-5472-85a2-1c589c3a076e.definition: Crafted by Zakariya' al-Qazwini in various Persian and Arabic editions in the years following the Mongol conquest and sack of Baghdad in AH 656  (1258 AD), 'Aja'ib al-makhluqat wa-ghara'ib al-mawjudat (The Wonders of Creation and the Oddities of Existence) emerged as the preeminent medieval compendium of natural history. The author's primary objective was to guide readers in recognising the omnipotence and benevolence of God by inspiring them to marvel at the astounding diversity within creation, and the remarkable perfection evident in all its celestial and terrestrial components.
spellings: The Wonders of Creation and the Oddities of Existence

9b57e731-19ab-55da-8b80-25d31d0f41c3.definition:
Arabic: “one-third”. A style of calligraphy named after the size of the pen used. The prolongation of its letters allow for very complex decorative compositions. It was used in calligraphy, books and civil and religious architecture. From the AH 12th / AD 18th century it was widely used in panels particular to Ottoman art. Fr. *toulouth*. Tr. *sülüs*.  
  
The thuluth script, a medieval Islamic calligraphic style, features an alphabet written in a distinctive manner. The name "thuluth" (Arabic for "one-third") refers to the principle that each letter's form encompasses a slope of about one-third of its size. This script is both spacious and refined, characterized by its cursive nature. During the medieval period, thuluth script found its place on mosque embellishments.  
Functionally, thuluth script assumed some of the roles initially held by the early Kufic script. It was employed for crafting headings for suras (chapters) of the Qurʾan, religious inscriptions, princely titles, and inscriptions of importance. Additionally, from the 13th century AD (597-700 AH) onwards, it was favoured for producing large copies of the Qurʾan.

59087726-c8e5-5434-aecc-5dd7d3e42d51.definition: A hard, quick-drying plaster processed from river silt used in Saharan building for making building blocks, as mortar, and for rendering.

a054eff3-ab33-572b-8c6c-47a7d300c111.definition: First used for embroidered inscriptions on textiles, this term became synonymous with textile robes with inscriptions giving the ruler’s name and the workshop where the textiles were made. Such robes were presented by the caliph to people who were to be honoured. Dar al-tiraz: royal textile factories supervised by the court.

9c8dfd7c-96f7-590d-8c3e-dacf904f0e4a.definition: A brass alloy usually referred to as red bronze. It is also mentioned as gilded copper and as a technique which uses copper and zinc alloy and gilt. Could also refer to tobacco.

1ad5b477-1036-5c86-ba62-687284025702.definition: Modern day Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, southern Kyrgyzstan and southwest Kazakhstan.

744d1b33-89fe-5377-a4fb-132f67bbf758.definition: Meaning "blessedness", a tree which grows in Jannah, also considered as the three of paradise.

5e33fb53-916f-516d-b614-5039d1c3c7ec.definition: A calligraphic signature of an Ottoman sultan that was affixed to official documents. Each sultan had his own *tughra*. Tr. *tuğra*.

84d9ad68-024a-5ca8-9f67-268e29d1e040.definition: A particular style of calligraphy, originating from India.

21c32408-3e62-5ec5-a0a4-ea90126bed70.definition: Turabi Bek Khurasani appears to be an artist, or possibly a collector, known for creating paintings that imitated and adapted various Persian painting styles. This artist's identity remains somewhat mysterious and may have been used for commercial purposes, potentially to cater to the tastes of collectors outside Iran. The paintings attributed to Turabi Bek Khurasani were designed to be perceived as genuine Safavid-period works, although they incorporated elements of both reproduction and selective adaptation. It is believed that there may have been an intention to deceive and profit from such deception, indicating a fraudulent aspect to these works. Turabi/Turabasi Bek Khurasani's creations were an attempt to blend traditional Persian painting practices with a contemporary approach for the sake of appealing to collectors in a different cultural context.

ce2219af-ca75-5d6e-a3b1-280a9ea04fbc.definition: Mausoleum, tomb, private burial place, sometimes with a crypt below, an architectural practice introduced by the Turks. Tr. *kümbet*, a monumental tomb, usually covered with a dome hidden under a spire. See also *darih*, *maqam*, *mashhad*, *qubba*.

5cc4d556-5ce6-575d-a50b-a403e6c59d4f.definition: A headdress consisting of a long scarf wound round the head or a smaller, underlying hat. Turbans vary in shape, colour, and size.

b6fc69ea-ced1-5b11-8e24-2ac2f4c53e76.definition: An architectural technique using triangles and chevrons to make the transition from square walls to a curved dome.

9d699883-6a5a-53ad-8a08-f3b27574c431.definition: Turkish people located in the region east of the Caspian Sea and South of the Aral Sea. This area now comprises of Turkmenistan and parts of Iran and Afghanistan.

fd4ff19f-5ca3-5bdd-b26e-79e1ad771914.definition:
"Turquoise is a blue-green gemstone made from hydrated copper aluminium phosphate. It between five and six on the Mohs scale, and is mainly cut in the cabochon style since it is not transparent. This gemstone comes in a variety of shades of blue and green. Turquoise was known in Egypt from a very early time and was later described by Pliny the Elder under the name *callias*. For him and those who studied his works, the blueish-green stone was attributed only virtues shared by other green or blue gems. However, in the 13th century, the term turquoise was introduced in Western Europe, and the gemstone started to be affiliated with new powers. These included the ability to prevent injuries from falling, especially from horseback, and the power to protect horses from sickness. For this reason Turks were said to attach turquoise stones to the bridles and stirrups of their horses.  
Turquoise has traditionally been sold in Turkey, since it mostly originates in Iran. It still passes through Turkey on the way to Europe. Ancient Persians fully appreciated the beauty and power of this gemstone, and it was the national stone of the vast empire. There is a saying that good fortune can be obtained by seeing the reflection of the new moon either on a friend’s face, on a copy of the Quran, or on a turquoise. Turquoise is also popular for religious use in Hindu mystic circles, as well as among Indigenous people of North and Central America."

04e377c7-df9e-578d-a9cd-de2fa4b2cef9.definition: Wooden cabinet of mixed Spanish and Oriental origin that first appeared in Europe in the late Middle Ages and became a common article of furniture in the Spanish colonial empire from the late 16th century onward. Its major component is a chest with a drop front. The interior is divided into an intricate arrangement of drawers and recesses for holding jewels, documents, and other valuables. The drawers and recesses are often inlaid with ivory, silver, or gold and are occasionally stained in bright colours. The exterior is elaborately mounted at the corners and elsewhere in iron or silver, and the front is secured by a heavy padlock or conventional lock.

eb1995df-c617-5ca0-95bc-cd6422ffca9a.definition: A variety of Islamic metalwork. Formerly believed to have been made by Muslim craftsmen in Venice, these objects are now thought to have been made mainly for Venetian merchants by Syrian craftsmen, with only a small number made in Italy. Their distinctive style includes heraldic emblems of European nobility.

577792e7-dcb2-5783-bc01-836c6f2cded6.definition: Minister. Tr. *vezir*. The highest vizier (Prime Minister) was the Grand Vizier, Prime Minister. Tr. *Sadrazam*.

fbb75391-7625-52c9-8a1c-5ab26a82c52c.definition: A deputy, delegate or agent who acts on behalf of a principal. It can refer to an attorney, a diplomat or the custodian of a mosque or religious order. Also, could mean prime minister.

38031924-6b4f-5fb1-9337-c0222f9b16d2.definition: Endowment in perpetuity, usually of land or property, from which the revenue was reserved for the upkeep of religious foundations. *waqfiyya*: the deed of endowment of a *waqf*. Tr. *vakıf*, *vakfiye*. See also *habus*.

9d0320cb-1068-5d1a-bb89-97a0628cb0f4.definition: Trading establishment with lodgings for merchants. See also *caravanserai*, *funduq*, *khan*.

cc1e247a-53d7-5c70-9399-89357963e5cf.definition: A style in Ottoman art which uses Chinoiserie decorations. The designs incorporate stylised lotus blossoms, buds and leaves in decorative scrolls. Hatayi is derived from Chatay in China. See also Chinoiserie.

c7ce411f-9d53-5566-8a9c-a1744854bc80.definition: An officer’s rank in the Turkish army. Tr. Ağa. See also *bey*, *dey*.

bcebf34c-f01e-5220-896e-b24e7d5c3220.definition: Hostel for merchants and their pack animals, a store for merchandise, a commercial centre. See also *caravanserai*, *khan*, *wikala*.

0a50d27f-efe1-5a2e-a5d7-61a78d619c48.definition: Turkish word for pillow or cushion.

e9d33609-b4fe-5b09-a0be-886bd0fc6c67.definition: A type of Ottoman knife or short sabre used from the mid-16th to late 19th centuries. The yataghan was extensively used in Ottoman Turkey and in areas under immediate Ottoman influence, such as the Balkans and the Caucasus.

19ba2374-d3c1-58b9-9a5e-7c9421eb5612.definition: A historic city in central Iran, renowned for its well-preserved mud-brick architecture and the ancient Zoroastrian fire temple, Atash Bahram. Yazd is situated in the desert and is also reputed for its distinct windcatcher towers (badgir) that provide natural ventilation in the city's buildings. It's a centre for Zoroastrian culture and has a rich history dating back thousands of years.

3be785b3-ebc7-5a4a-80b6-6cf2786cd3a5.definition: A vest, usually sleeveless. Can vary in length, depending on province.

babd8299-36a4-5030-94fb-4d24368825d6.definition: Abu Yahya Zakariya ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmud al-Qazwini (AH 599- 680 / AD 1203-1282) was a Persian polymath with expertise in medicine, astronomy, and geography. He was born in Qazwin and undertook extensive travels in regions such as Mesopotamia and the Levant. He dedicated his work on cosmography, titled 'Aja'ib al-Makhluqat wa Ghara'ib al-Maujudat, to 'Ata-Malik Juwayni (d. AH 681 / AD 1283), a Persian historian who, following the sack of Baghdad in AH 656 / AD 1258, was appointed as governor of the city by the Mongol ruler Hulaqu.

00cb9155-a05e-57be-b845-f2828bcd7de6.definition: Another of the five pillars of Islam, Zakat is a tithe that is to be paid each year by all Muslim adults in the amount of 2.5 percent of their income and wealth.

c820b0fc-daf0-5f36-aed6-5dcb2aab4aa8.definition: Sharp plane, also is considered a technique used to separate the lines of text within the panel.

76676210-58c4-5de1-89e6-594e4175ceac.definition: Establishment for religious teaching dedicated to preparing men to become *shaykhs*, which includes the shrine of a saint and built where he was born or lived. In Turkey also a small *tekke*, a hospice for dervishes and travellers. See also *khanqah*, *tekke*, *takiyya*.

9aa57c3b-8983-5efb-9663-8813a2e47d5c.definition: Small glazed ceramic tiles or cut-out parts of tiles set like mosaics to form a complex geometric design in interiors and exteriors of buildings. Fr. *zellige*.

5d4dc8f2-b5cd-50de-a181-37e249c0c934.definition: Used by the inhabitants of Rashid (Rosetta) for ceramic tiles, as it is derived from the word, zillij meaning ceramic tiles in colloquial Maghrebi Arabic.

b2664e35-a30a-5283-80bf-77beed25e898.definition: The empty space between the walls of a building (for example, a mosque) and an outer wall.

112111b5-7829-509e-a270-9ff69b2a9c0d.definition: A type of knee- length tunic.
